------------------------------ MODULE W4Od8m6p2t5 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Students, TotalSeats, LeaseSpan, Horizon

\* Seat entitlements are a conserved quantity: every seat sits in exactly one
\* of three places -- the registrar bank, a student's unconfirmed lease, or a
\* student's confirmed enrolment. No action may mint or shred a seat.

RECURSIVE Tally(_, _)
Tally(f, S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET pick == CHOOSE s \in S : TRUE
       IN f[pick] + Tally(f, S \ {pick})

VARIABLES bank, onLease, seated, expiresAt, wallClock
regVars == <<bank, onLease, seated, expiresAt, wallClock>>

Idle(s) == onLease[s] = 0 /\ seated[s] = 0
LeaseLive(s) == onLease[s] = 1 /\ wallClock =< expiresAt[s]
LeaseStale(s) == onLease[s] = 1 /\ wallClock > expiresAt[s]

TypeOK ==
  /\ bank \in 0 .. TotalSeats
  /\ onLease \in [Students -> 0 .. 1]
  /\ seated \in [Students -> 0 .. 1]
  /\ expiresAt \in [Students -> 0 .. (Horizon + LeaseSpan)]
  /\ wallClock \in 0 .. Horizon

Init ==
  /\ bank = TotalSeats
  /\ onLease = [s \in Students |-> 0]
  /\ seated = [s \in Students |-> 0]
  /\ expiresAt = [s \in Students |-> 0]
  /\ wallClock = 0

\* A seat leaves the bank and becomes a time-limited hold on one student.
OfferLease(s) ==
  /\ bank > 0
  /\ Idle(s)
  /\ bank' = bank - 1
  /\ onLease' = [onLease EXCEPT ![s] = 1]
  /\ expiresAt' = [expiresAt EXCEPT ![s] = wallClock + LeaseSpan]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seated, wallClock>>

\* The hold turns into a real seat; the seat itself never touches the bank.
ConfirmSeat(s) ==
  /\ LeaseLive(s)
  /\ onLease' = [onLease EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
  /\ seated' = [seated EXCEPT ![s] = 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bank, expiresAt, wallClock>>

\* Expiry hands the seat straight back to the registrar bank.
ReapExpired(s) ==
  /\ LeaseStale(s)
  /\ onLease' = [onLease EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
  /\ bank' = bank + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<seated, expiresAt, wallClock>>

\* Privileged override: the registrar may pull a confirmed enrolment at any
\* time, ignoring lease timing entirely, but the seat still returns to stock.
AdminRescind(s) ==
  /\ seated[s] = 1
  /\ seated' = [seated EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
  /\ bank' = bank + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<onLease, expiresAt, wallClock>>

AdvanceClock ==
  /\ wallClock < Horizon
  /\ wallClock' = wallClock + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bank, onLease, seated, expiresAt>>

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in Students : OfferLease(s)
  \/ \E s \in Students : ConfirmSeat(s)
  \/ \E s \in Students : ReapExpired(s)
  \/ \E s \in Students : AdminRescind(s)
  \/ AdvanceClock

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_regVars

SeatsConserved ==
  bank + Tally(onLease, Students) + Tally(seated, Students) = TotalSeats
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Students = {alice, bo, cy}
    TotalSeats = 3
    LeaseSpan = 1
    Horizon = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT SeatsConserved
nl:
A university runs course registration against a fixed stock of seat entitlements for one popular course. The registrar keeps every unallocated seat in a central bank. When a student starts registering, the system moves one seat out of the bank and onto that student as a time-limited lease: the lease records a wall-clock expiry a fixed span into the future. A student who already holds a lease or is already seated cannot be offered another one.

While the lease is still live -- the wall clock has not passed its expiry -- the student may confirm, which turns the hold into a confirmed enrolment. Confirming does not touch the bank at all; the seat simply changes hands from the lease column to the enrolment column. If instead the wall clock passes the expiry before confirmation, the seat is reaped: the lease is torn down and the seat goes straight back into the registrar bank so somebody else can take it.

There is one privileged path. The registrar has an administrative override and may rescind any confirmed enrolment at any moment, regardless of lease timing or of whether the student agrees. When the override fires, the enrolment is cancelled and that seat is returned to the bank exactly like an expired lease would have been. The wall clock advances on its own up to a fixed horizon, which is what makes leases go stale.

The full action set is: offer a lease on a banked seat to an idle student, confirm a live lease into an enrolment, reap a lease whose expiry has passed and return its seat to the bank, apply the administrative override to rescind a confirmed enrolment and return its seat to the bank, and advance the wall clock.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of seats in the registrar bank plus the number held on leases plus the number held as confirmed enrolments always equals the fixed total stock of seats, so no seat entitlement is ever created or destroyed by leasing, expiry, confirmation, or the administrative override.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od6m5p5t4 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cars, Controllers, QuorumSize, MaxOutOfService

\* Retiring an elevator car cuts its hoist rope: physically irreversible.
\* A retirement needs QuorumSize controllers on that car's ballot; a cast vote
\* is binding, so ballots only ever grow while the car is balloting.

VARIABLES stance, ballot, retireOrder, orderIndex, outCap
bankVars == <<stance, ballot, retireOrder, orderIndex, outCap>>

Balloting == {c \in Cars : stance[c] = "balloting"}
HasQuorum(c) == Cardinality(ballot[c]) >= QuorumSize

TypeOK ==
  /\ stance \in [Cars -> {"running", "balloting", "retired"}]
  /\ ballot \in [Cars -> SUBSET Controllers]
  /\ orderIndex \in [Cars -> 0 .. Cardinality(Cars)]
  /\ outCap \in 1 .. MaxOutOfService

Init ==
  /\ stance = [c \in Cars |-> "running"]
  /\ ballot = [c \in Cars |-> {}]
  /\ retireOrder = <<>>
  /\ orderIndex = [c \in Cars |-> 0]
  /\ outCap = 1

\* The bank supervisor raises or lowers, at runtime, how many cars may be
\* under a retirement ballot at the same time.
Resize ==
  /\ \E n \in 1 .. MaxOutOfService : n # outCap /\ outCap' = n
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stance, ballot, retireOrder, orderIndex>>

OpenBallot(c) ==
  /\ stance[c] = "running"
  /\ Cardinality(Balloting) < outCap
  /\ stance' = [stance EXCEPT ![c] = "balloting"]
  /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![c] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<retireOrder, orderIndex, outCap>>

CastVote(c, k) ==
  /\ stance[c] = "balloting"
  /\ k \notin ballot[c]
  /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![c] = ballot[c] \cup {k}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stance, retireOrder, orderIndex, outCap>>

\* Housekeeping: once the order book line is filed the paper ballot slip is
\* shredded. This never touches a car that is still balloting.
ShredSlip(c) ==
  /\ stance[c] = "retired"
  /\ ballot[c] # {}
  /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![c] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stance, retireOrder, orderIndex, outCap>>

\* The one irreversible step. It also files a witness: the car remembers the
\* position of its own line in the bank's retirement order book.
CommitRetire(c) ==
  /\ stance[c] = "balloting"
  /\ HasQuorum(c)
  /\ stance' = [stance EXCEPT ![c] = "retired"]
  /\ retireOrder' = Append(retireOrder, c)
  /\ orderIndex' = [orderIndex EXCEPT ![c] = Len(retireOrder) + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, outCap>>

AnyVote == \E c \in Cars, k \in Controllers : CastVote(c, k)
AnyRetire == \E c \in Cars : CommitRetire(c)

Next ==
  \/ Resize
  \/ \E c \in Cars : OpenBallot(c)
  \/ AnyVote
  \/ \E c \in Cars : ShredSlip(c)
  \/ AnyRetire

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_bankVars
  /\ WF_bankVars(AnyVote)
  /\ WF_bankVars(AnyRetire)

\* Every line of the order book is claimed by the car that remembers standing
\* exactly there; a car cut twice would leave its earlier line unclaimed.
OrderBookWitnessed ==
  \A i \in 1 .. Len(retireOrder) : orderIndex[retireOrder[i]] = i

BallotSettles ==
  \A c \in Cars : (stance[c] = "balloting") ~> (stance[c] = "retired")
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Cars = {carA, carB}
    Controllers = {sup1, sup2, sup3}
    QuorumSize = 2
    MaxOutOfService = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT OrderBookWitnessed

PROPERTY BallotSettles
nl:
A skyscraper's elevator bank is supervised by a small group of controllers. Cars normally run. Taking a car out permanently means cutting its hoist rope and craning it out of the shaft, which is irreversible: a retired car can never be put back into the bank, and the rope cannot be uncut. Because the step is irreversible, no single controller may order it; the bank uses quorum voting.

A car is first moved from running into balloting, which opens a fresh, empty ballot for it. Controllers then cast votes onto that car's ballot. A cast vote is binding and cannot be taken back, so an open ballot only ever grows. The retirement order may be committed once the required number of controllers are holding votes on that car. Committing writes a new line into the bank's retirement order book, in order, and the car itself records which line of the order book is its own. After the line has been filed, the paper ballot slip for that retired car is shredded as housekeeping; shredding never touches a car that is still balloting.

The bank's tolerance for out-of-service cars is not fixed. The supervisor may raise or lower, at runtime, how many cars are allowed to be under a retirement ballot at the same time, and a new ballot may only be opened while the number of cars currently balloting is below that limit. Resizing never disturbs a ballot that is already open.

The full action set is: resize the out-of-service limit, open a ballot on a running car when the limit allows, cast a binding controller vote onto an open ballot, commit the retirement of a car whose ballot holds a quorum, and shred the ballot slip of an already-retired car.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every line of the retirement order book is claimed by the car that records standing at exactly that line, so a car cut out of the bank twice would leave its earlier line unclaimed and the claim never holds twice.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every car that enters balloting is eventually retired.

spec_text:
------------------------------ MODULE W4Od16m8p1t2 -----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Dispensers, Drawers, MaxRevision

None == "none"

\* Two dispenser instances share one drawer pool. To edit a drawer's dispense
\* ledger an instance takes the coarse pool latch first, pins the fine drawer
\* latch under it, then drops the pool latch (classic latch coupling).

VARIABLES poolLatch, drawerLatch, phase, aimedAt, snapshot, revision
dispVars == <<poolLatch, drawerLatch, phase, aimedAt, snapshot, revision>>

Busy == {"scanning", "pinned", "staged", "editing"}
HoldsPool(i) == poolLatch = i
HoldsDrawer(i) == aimedAt[i] # None /\ drawerLatch[aimedAt[i]] = i

TypeOK ==
  /\ poolLatch \in Dispensers \cup {None}
  /\ drawerLatch \in [Drawers -> Dispensers \cup {None}]
  /\ phase \in [Dispensers -> {"idle"} \cup Busy]
  /\ aimedAt \in [Dispensers -> Drawers \cup {None}]
  /\ snapshot \in [Dispensers -> 0 .. MaxRevision]
  /\ revision \in [Drawers -> 0 .. MaxRevision]

Init ==
  /\ poolLatch = None
  /\ drawerLatch = [d \in Drawers |-> None]
  /\ phase = [i \in Dispensers |-> "idle"]
  /\ aimedAt = [i \in Dispensers |-> None]
  /\ snapshot = [i \in Dispensers |-> 0]
  /\ revision = [d \in Drawers |-> 0]

TakePoolLatch(i) ==
  /\ phase[i] = "idle"
  /\ poolLatch = None
  /\ poolLatch' = i
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![i] = "scanning"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<drawerLatch, aimedAt, snapshot, revision>>

PinDrawer(i, d) ==
  /\ phase[i] = "scanning"
  /\ drawerLatch[d] = None
  /\ drawerLatch' = [drawerLatch EXCEPT ![d] = i]
  /\ aimedAt' = [aimedAt EXCEPT ![i] = d]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![i] = "pinned"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<poolLatch, snapshot, revision>>

DropPoolLatch(i) ==
  /\ phase[i] = "pinned"
  /\ poolLatch' = None
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![i] = "staged"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<drawerLatch, aimedAt, snapshot, revision>>

\* The read-modify-write window opens here: the instance copies the drawer's
\* revision stamp and works off that copy until it writes back.
ReadLedger(i) ==
  /\ phase[i] = "staged"
  /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![i] = revision[aimedAt[i]]]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![i] = "editing"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<poolLatch, drawerLatch, aimedAt, revision>>

WriteBack(i) ==
  /\ phase[i] = "editing"
  /\ revision[aimedAt[i]] < MaxRevision
  /\ revision' = [revision EXCEPT ![aimedAt[i]] = snapshot[i] + 1]
  /\ drawerLatch' = [drawerLatch EXCEPT ![aimedAt[i]] = None]
  /\ aimedAt' = [aimedAt EXCEPT ![i] = None]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![i] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<poolLatch, snapshot>>

\* A pharmacist can cancel mid-way; every latch the instance holds comes off.
Abandon(i) ==
  /\ phase[i] \in Busy
  /\ poolLatch' = IF HoldsPool(i) THEN None ELSE poolLatch
  /\ drawerLatch' = IF HoldsDrawer(i)
                    THEN [drawerLatch EXCEPT ![aimedAt[i]] = None]
                    ELSE drawerLatch
  /\ aimedAt' = [aimedAt EXCEPT ![i] = None]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![i] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<snapshot, revision>>

Next ==
  \/ \E i \in Dispensers : TakePoolLatch(i)
  \/ \E i \in Dispensers, d \in Drawers : PinDrawer(i, d)
  \/ \E i \in Dispensers : DropPoolLatch(i)
  \/ \E i \in Dispensers : ReadLedger(i)
  \/ \E i \in Dispensers : WriteBack(i)
  \/ \E i \in Dispensers : Abandon(i)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_dispVars

\* No lost update: while an instance is mid-edit the drawer's live revision is
\* still exactly the one it read, so its write-back cannot paper over another
\* instance's write.
EditsNeverGoStale ==
  \A i \in Dispensers :
    phase[i] = "editing" => snapshot[i] = revision[aimedAt[i]]
================================================================================
nl:
A hospital pharmacy runs two prescription-dispensing cabinets as independent instances of the same machine, but both draw from a single shared pool of medication drawers. Every drawer carries a dispense ledger whose revision stamp is bumped each time the drawer's contents are written back.

Editing a drawer's ledger goes through a two-level latch discipline. An idle cabinet first takes the coarse pool latch, which is a single latch over the whole shared drawer pool, and starts scanning. While scanning it pins the fine latch of one particular drawer that is not already pinned by the other cabinet. Once the fine latch is pinned the cabinet drops the coarse pool latch, so the other cabinet is free to come in and work on a different drawer; the coarse latch is only ever used to get safely down to a fine latch.

With only the drawer's fine latch in hand, the cabinet reads the drawer's revision stamp into a local snapshot and begins editing off that copy. When it writes back, it stores a revision derived from the snapshot it read, and then releases the drawer's fine latch. A pharmacist may also cancel the operation at any point while the cabinet is busy, in which case every latch that cabinet is currently holding -- pool latch, drawer latch, or both -- comes off and the cabinet returns to idle without writing anything. Ledger revisions do not grow without bound; a drawer at its maximum revision must be cancelled rather than written back.

The full action set is: take the coarse pool latch, pin a free drawer's fine latch while scanning, drop the coarse pool latch once a drawer is pinned, read the pinned drawer's revision stamp into a snapshot, write back a new revision and release the drawer latch, and cancel a busy cabinet by releasing every latch it holds.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a cabinet is in the middle of editing, the live revision stamp of the drawer it has pinned is still exactly the snapshot it read, so no write-back can ever silently overwrite an update made by the other cabinet in between.

spec_text:
------------------------------ MODULE W4Od3m0p2t3 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS NumBanks, Endowment, Leg

Banks == 0 .. (NumBanks - 1)
Downstream(b) == (b + 1) % NumBanks
TotalFunds == NumBanks * Endowment

\* Optimistic settlement: a bank copies the batch ledger's version stamp, and
\* its debit only lands if the stamp still matches. A losing bank re-reads or
\* restarts -- it is slow, never dead -- and tries the same leg again.

RECURSIVE Pile(_, _, _)
Pile(g, dom, acc) ==
  IF dom = {} THEN acc
  ELSE LET b == CHOOSE x \in dom : TRUE
       IN Pile(g, dom \ {b}, acc + g[b])

VARIABLES vault, inFlight, legStage, stampSeen, batchStamp
setVars == <<vault, inFlight, legStage, stampSeen, batchStamp>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ vault \in [Banks -> 0 .. (2 * Endowment)]
  /\ inFlight \in [Banks -> 0 .. Leg]
  /\ legStage \in [Banks -> {"fresh", "read", "moving", "settled"}]
  /\ stampSeen \in [Banks -> 0 .. NumBanks]
  /\ batchStamp \in 0 .. NumBanks

Init ==
  /\ vault = [b \in Banks |-> Endowment]
  /\ inFlight = [b \in Banks |-> 0]
  /\ legStage = [b \in Banks |-> "fresh"]
  /\ stampSeen = [b \in Banks |-> 0]
  /\ batchStamp = 0

OpenRead(b) ==
  /\ legStage[b] = "fresh"
  /\ stampSeen' = [stampSeen EXCEPT ![b] = batchStamp]
  /\ legStage' = [legStage EXCEPT ![b] = "read"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<vault, inFlight, batchStamp>>

\* Cheap retry: refresh the stamp in place after somebody else committed.
Refresh(b) ==
  /\ legStage[b] = "read"
  /\ stampSeen[b] # batchStamp
  /\ stampSeen' = [stampSeen EXCEPT ![b] = batchStamp]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<vault, inFlight, legStage, batchStamp>>

\* Expensive retry: throw the whole attempt away and start from scratch.
Restart(b) ==
  /\ legStage[b] = "read"
  /\ stampSeen[b] # batchStamp
  /\ legStage' = [legStage EXCEPT ![b] = "fresh"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<vault, inFlight, stampSeen, batchStamp>>

\* Debit half of the leg: money leaves the vault into the in-flight column.
DebitLeg(b) ==
  /\ legStage[b] = "read"
  /\ stampSeen[b] = batchStamp
  /\ vault[b] >= Leg
  /\ vault' = [vault EXCEPT ![b] = vault[b] - Leg]
  /\ inFlight' = [inFlight EXCEPT ![b] = Leg]
  /\ batchStamp' = batchStamp + 1
  /\ legStage' = [legStage EXCEPT ![b] = "moving"]
  /\ UNCHANGED stampSeen

\* Credit half: the same money lands downstream and leaves the in-flight column.
CreditLeg(b) ==
  /\ legStage[b] = "moving"
  /\ vault' = [vault EXCEPT ![Downstream(b)] = vault[Downstream(b)] + inFlight[b]]
  /\ inFlight' = [inFlight EXCEPT ![b] = 0]
  /\ legStage' = [legStage EXCEPT ![b] = "settled"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stampSeen, batchStamp>>

\* When every leg is settled the batch is closed and the clearing house idles.
BatchClosed == \A b \in Banks : legStage[b] = "settled"
Idle == BatchClosed /\ UNCHANGED setVars

AnyOpen == \E b \in Banks : OpenRead(b)
AnyRefresh == \E b \in Banks : Refresh(b)
AnyDebit == \E b \in Banks : DebitLeg(b)
AnyCredit == \E b \in Banks : CreditLeg(b)

Next ==
  \/ AnyOpen
  \/ AnyRefresh
  \/ \E b \in Banks : Restart(b)
  \/ AnyDebit
  \/ AnyCredit
  \/ Idle

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_setVars
  /\ WF_setVars(AnyOpen)
  /\ WF_setVars(AnyRefresh)
  /\ WF_setVars(AnyCredit)
  /\ SF_setVars(AnyDebit)

\* Money is only ever in a vault or in the in-flight column, never anywhere else.
FundsConserved ==
  Pile(vault, Banks, 0) + Pile(inFlight, Banks, 0) = TotalFunds

EveryLegSettles ==
  \A b \in Banks : (legStage[b] # "settled") ~> (legStage[b] = "settled")
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    NumBanks = 3
    Endowment = 1
    Leg = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT FundsConserved

PROPERTY EveryLegSettles
nl:
A clearing house settles a nightly interbank batch. The banks are arranged in a cycle, and each bank owes exactly one leg of a fixed size to its downstream neighbour. Every bank starts the night with the same endowment in its vault. The batch ledger carries a single version stamp that is bumped every time a leg is debited.

Settlement is optimistic rather than locked. A bank first opens a read, copying the batch ledger's current version stamp into its own working copy. It may then debit its leg, but only if the stamp it copied still matches the ledger's live stamp; if somebody else got in first, the copied stamp is stale and the debit is refused. A bank that finds itself stale has two ways to retry: it can refresh its copied stamp in place and try again, or it can throw the whole attempt away and start over from a fresh read. Banks in this batch are slow, not failed -- a bank may take arbitrarily long between steps, but it never stops trying.

A debit does not deliver the money in one step. The debit takes the leg amount out of the paying bank's vault and parks it in that bank's in-flight column, and bumps the ledger stamp. The matching credit later moves the same amount out of the in-flight column and into the downstream neighbour's vault, at which point that bank's leg is settled. A settled leg is never reopened.

Once every bank's leg has settled the batch is closed and the clearing house simply idles until morning.

The full action set is: open a read that copies the ledger stamp, refresh a stale copied stamp in place, restart a stale attempt from scratch, debit the leg into the in-flight column while the copied stamp still matches and bump the ledger stamp, credit the in-flight amount into the downstream bank's vault, and idle once the batch is closed.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The money sitting in bank vaults plus the money sitting in in-flight columns always adds up to exactly the total endowed at the start of the batch, so settlement never creates or destroys funds even when reads go stale and legs are retried.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every bank's leg is eventually settled, no matter how many times its optimistic read loses the race.

spec_text:
------------------------------ MODULE W4Od2m9p5t1 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Drones, Cages, MaxEpoch

\* Cutting a cage's shipping band is irreversible. Orders travel over a radio
\* mesh that reorders and holds messages, so the fleet leans entirely on epoch
\* fences: each cage accepts an order stamped with exactly its own fence, and
\* the fence steps forward the moment the band is cut.

Orders == [cage : Cages, drone : Drones, ep : 0 .. MaxEpoch]

VARIABLES fleetEpoch, fence, band, adopted, mesh
fleetVars == <<fleetEpoch, fence, band, adopted, mesh>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ fleetEpoch \in 1 .. MaxEpoch
  /\ fence \in [Cages -> 0 .. (MaxEpoch + 1)]
  /\ band \in [Cages -> {"intact", "cut"}]
  /\ adopted \in [Drones -> 0 .. MaxEpoch]
  /\ mesh \subseteq Orders

Init ==
  /\ fleetEpoch = 1
  /\ fence = [g \in Cages |-> 0]
  /\ band = [g \in Cages |-> "intact"]
  /\ adopted = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
  /\ mesh = {}

\* Reconfiguration: the fleet controller opens a new epoch.
Reconfigure ==
  /\ fleetEpoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ fleetEpoch' = fleetEpoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fence, band, adopted, mesh>>

AdoptEpoch(d) ==
  /\ adopted[d] < fleetEpoch
  /\ adopted' = [adopted EXCEPT ![d] = fleetEpoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fleetEpoch, fence, band, mesh>>

\* Issuing an order raises the cage's fence to the issuing epoch, which is what
\* retires every order the controller sent for that cage in an older epoch.
IssueCut(g, d) ==
  /\ band[g] = "intact"
  /\ fence[g] < fleetEpoch
  /\ fence' = [fence EXCEPT ![g] = fleetEpoch]
  /\ mesh' = mesh \cup {[cage |-> g, drone |-> d, ep |-> fleetEpoch]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fleetEpoch, band, adopted>>

\* A drone obeys only an order stamped at the cage's live fence, and only if it
\* has caught up to that epoch. Cutting pushes the fence one past the order.
ExecuteCut(m) ==
  /\ m \in mesh
  /\ m.ep = fence[m.cage]
  /\ adopted[m.drone] >= m.ep
  /\ band' = [band EXCEPT ![m.cage] = "cut"]
  /\ fence' = [fence EXCEPT ![m.cage] = m.ep + 1]
  /\ mesh' = mesh \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fleetEpoch, adopted>>

\* Orders that no longer match their cage's fence are dropped on the floor.
DiscardStale(m) ==
  /\ m \in mesh
  /\ m.ep # fence[m.cage]
  /\ mesh' = mesh \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fleetEpoch, fence, band, adopted>>

Quiesce ==
  /\ fleetEpoch = MaxEpoch
  /\ mesh = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED fleetVars

Next ==
  \/ Reconfigure
  \/ \E d \in Drones : AdoptEpoch(d)
  \/ \E g \in Cages, d \in Drones : IssueCut(g, d)
  \/ \E m \in Orders : ExecuteCut(m)
  \/ \E m \in Orders : DiscardStale(m)
  \/ Quiesce

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_fleetVars

\* Once a band has been cut, every order still floating in the mesh for that
\* cage is strictly behind the cage's fence, so no surviving or reordered copy
\* can ever drive a second cut.
NoEncoreOrderSurvives ==
  \A m \in mesh : band[m.cage] = "cut" => m.ep < fence[m.cage]
================================================================================
nl:
A warehouse runs a fleet of autonomous floor robots that service shipping cages. Cutting a cage's steel shipping band is irreversible: the band is destroyed and the cage's contents are exposed, and there is no way to put a band back on. Orders travel from the fleet controller to the robots over a radio mesh that is unreliable in one specific way -- it never invents or corrupts an order, but it may hold an order for an arbitrary time and deliver orders in any sequence, so an old order can surface long after a newer one has already been acted on.

Because of that reordering, the fleet relies on epoch fences rather than on delivery order. The controller works in numbered epochs and may open a new epoch at any time; robots individually catch up to the controller's current epoch when they hear from it. Each cage carries its own fence number. When the controller issues a cut order for a cage that still has its band, it stamps the order with the current epoch and simultaneously raises that cage's fence to the same number, which is exactly what retires every order it sent for that cage in an earlier epoch. The controller only issues an order for a cage whose fence is behind the current epoch.

A robot obeys a cut order only when the order's stamp matches the cage's live fence and the robot has itself caught up to at least that epoch. Carrying out the cut destroys the band and pushes the cage's fence one step past the order that was just obeyed. Any order whose stamp does not match its cage's fence is simply dropped on the floor by whichever robot picks it up. When the controller has reached its final epoch and the mesh is empty, the fleet sits quiet.

The full action set is: open a new epoch, let a robot catch up to the controller's epoch, issue a fence-raising cut order for a banded cage, execute a cut order whose stamp matches the cage's fence, discard an order whose stamp does not match its cage's fence, and sit quiet once the final epoch is reached and the mesh has drained.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every cage whose band has already been cut, every order still floating in the radio mesh for that cage carries a stamp strictly behind the cage's current fence, so no delayed or out-of-order copy can ever drive a second cut of the same band.

spec_text:
----------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m2p4t3 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Trains, NumBlocks, BlockCap

Blocks == 0 .. (NumBlocks - 1)
Route(h) == {h, (h + 1) % NumBlocks}
Nowhere == NumBlocks

\* A train's route spans two adjacent blocks, and each block controller is a
\* separate participant in the interlocking's two-phase commit. A controller
\* answers whenever it gets round to it -- late is fine, silent is not.
\* A prepare reserves headroom, so a held claim eats capacity before the train
\* ever rolls onto the block.

VARIABLES leg, headBlock, granted, reserved, wheels
sigVars == <<leg, headBlock, granted, reserved, wheels>>

MyRoute(t) == Route(headBlock[t])
Loaded(b) == reserved[b] + wheels[b]

TypeOK ==
  /\ leg \in [Trains -> {"stabled", "polling", "rolling"}]
  /\ headBlock \in [Trains -> Blocks \cup {Nowhere}]
  /\ granted \in [Trains -> SUBSET Blocks]
  /\ reserved \in [Blocks -> 0 .. BlockCap]
  /\ wheels \in [Blocks -> 0 .. BlockCap]

Init ==
  /\ leg = [t \in Trains |-> "stabled"]
  /\ headBlock = [t \in Trains |-> Nowhere]
  /\ granted = [t \in Trains |-> {}]
  /\ reserved = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
  /\ wheels = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]

RequestRoute(t, h) ==
  /\ leg[t] = "stabled"
  /\ leg' = [leg EXCEPT ![t] = "polling"]
  /\ headBlock' = [headBlock EXCEPT ![t] = h]
  /\ granted' = [granted EXCEPT ![t] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reserved, wheels>>

\* A block controller votes yes by booking headroom for the asking train.
VoteYes(t, b) ==
  /\ leg[t] = "polling"
  /\ b \in MyRoute(t)
  /\ b \notin granted[t]
  /\ Loaded(b) < BlockCap
  /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![b] = reserved[b] + 1]
  /\ granted' = [granted EXCEPT ![t] = granted[t] \cup {b}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leg, headBlock, wheels>>

\* Commit converts every booked reservation into a real occupancy in one step.
CommitRoute(t) ==
  /\ leg[t] = "polling"
  /\ granted[t] = MyRoute(t)
  /\ reserved' = [b \in Blocks |->
       IF b \in MyRoute(t) THEN reserved[b] - 1 ELSE reserved[b]]
  /\ wheels' = [b \in Blocks |->
       IF b \in MyRoute(t) THEN wheels[b] + 1 ELSE wheels[b]]
  /\ leg' = [leg EXCEPT ![t] = "rolling"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<headBlock, granted>>

\* If some controller on the route has no headroom left, the whole route is
\* rolled back and every reservation already booked for it is handed back.
AbortRoute(t) ==
  /\ leg[t] = "polling"
  /\ \E b \in MyRoute(t) : b \notin granted[t] /\ Loaded(b) >= BlockCap
  /\ reserved' = [b \in Blocks |->
       IF b \in granted[t] THEN reserved[b] - 1 ELSE reserved[b]]
  /\ granted' = [granted EXCEPT ![t] = {}]
  /\ headBlock' = [headBlock EXCEPT ![t] = Nowhere]
  /\ leg' = [leg EXCEPT ![t] = "stabled"]
  /\ UNCHANGED wheels

ClearRoute(t) ==
  /\ leg[t] = "rolling"
  /\ wheels' = [b \in Blocks |->
       IF b \in MyRoute(t) THEN wheels[b] - 1 ELSE wheels[b]]
  /\ granted' = [granted EXCEPT ![t] = {}]
  /\ headBlock' = [headBlock EXCEPT ![t] = Nowhere]
  /\ leg' = [leg EXCEPT ![t] = "stabled"]
  /\ UNCHANGED reserved

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Trains, h \in Blocks : RequestRoute(t, h)
  \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : VoteYes(t, b)
  \/ \E t \in Trains : CommitRoute(t)
  \/ \E t \in Trains : AbortRoute(t)
  \/ \E t \in Trains : ClearRoute(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_sigVars

\* Capacity is charged at prepare time, not at commit time: the axles already
\* standing on a block plus the outstanding reservations booked against it
\* never together exceed what the block is rated to hold.
BlockNeverOverbooked ==
  \A b \in Blocks : wheels[b] + reserved[b] <= BlockCap
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Trains = {t1, t2}
    NumBlocks = 3
    BlockCap = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT BlockNeverOverbooked
nl:
A subway line is divided into signalling blocks arranged around a loop. Each block is rated to hold a fixed number of trains at once, and each block has its own controller. A train that wants to move must take a route spanning two adjacent blocks -- the head block it names and the one immediately after it -- so every route needs the agreement of two separate block controllers. The interlocking gets that agreement with two-phase commit. The block controllers are slow, not failed: a controller may take arbitrarily long to answer a poll, but it always answers eventually and never drops out of the protocol.

A stabled train opens a route request by naming a head block and starting to poll; nothing is booked yet. Each controller on the route votes yes by booking headroom for that train on its own block, but only if the block is not already at its rating counting both the trains standing on it and the reservations already booked against it. Capacity is therefore charged at prepare time, before any train rolls: a booked reservation eats a block's rating just as much as an axle does.

When every controller on the route has voted yes, the interlocking commits, and in that one step every reservation held for the route turns into a real occupancy on the corresponding block. If a controller on the route finds its block has no headroom left, the whole route is rolled back: every reservation already booked for that train is handed back to its block and the train returns to stabled with no route. A rolling train later clears its route, giving back the occupancy on both blocks and returning to stabled, from where it may request another route.

The full action set is: request a route by naming a head block and start polling, vote yes on one block of a polling train's route by booking headroom there, commit a route whose whole set of controllers has voted yes and turn its reservations into occupancies, abort a route when some controller on it has no headroom left and hand back every reservation booked for it, and clear a rolling train's route by giving back its occupancies.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every block, the trains standing on it plus the reservations still booked against it never together exceed the number of trains that block is rated to hold.

----------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m4p1t3 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS NumPosts, QueueCap

Posts == 1 .. NumPosts

\* Every signal post rewrites one field of the centre's shared occupancy board.
\* Rewrites travel through a bounded hand-off queue; the queue exerts back
\* pressure by refusing anything once it is full. A post reads the queue's tail
\* version and may only lodge a rewrite while that version is still the tail,
\* so the rewrites in the queue form one unbroken version chain.

VARIABLES stamp, queue, posture, tailSeen, board
centreVars == <<stamp, queue, posture, tailSeen, board>>

TailVersion == stamp + Len(queue)

TypeOK ==
  /\ stamp \in 0 .. NumPosts
  /\ posture \in [Posts -> {"quiet", "reading", "lodged", "written"}]
  /\ tailSeen \in [Posts -> 0 .. NumPosts]
  /\ board \in [Posts -> 0 .. 1]

Init ==
  /\ stamp = 0
  /\ queue = <<>>
  /\ posture = [p \in Posts |-> "quiet"]
  /\ tailSeen = [p \in Posts |-> 0]
  /\ board = [p \in Posts |-> 0]

\* The post reads which version its rewrite would land on.
StartRead(p) ==
  /\ posture[p] = "quiet"
  /\ tailSeen' = [tailSeen EXCEPT ![p] = TailVersion]
  /\ posture' = [posture EXCEPT ![p] = "reading"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stamp, queue, board>>

\* Somebody else got in first, so the version the post read is no longer the
\* tail; it takes a fresh reading rather than lodging a rewrite blind.
Reread(p) ==
  /\ posture[p] = "reading"
  /\ tailSeen[p] # TailVersion
  /\ tailSeen' = [tailSeen EXCEPT ![p] = TailVersion]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stamp, queue, posture, board>>

\* Back pressure: nothing goes in while the hand-off queue is at its cap.
Lodge(p) ==
  /\ posture[p] = "reading"
  /\ tailSeen[p] = TailVersion
  /\ Len(queue) < QueueCap
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, [post |-> p, base |-> tailSeen[p]])
  /\ posture' = [posture EXCEPT ![p] = "lodged"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stamp, tailSeen, board>>

ApplyHead ==
  /\ Len(queue) > 0
  /\ Head(queue).base = stamp
  /\ board' = [board EXCEPT ![Head(queue).post] = 1]
  /\ posture' = [posture EXCEPT ![Head(queue).post] = "written"]
  /\ stamp' = stamp + 1
  /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
  /\ UNCHANGED tailSeen

Settled == \A p \in Posts : posture[p] = "written"
Rest == Settled /\ UNCHANGED centreVars

AnyRead == \E p \in Posts : StartRead(p)
AnyReread == \E p \in Posts : Reread(p)
AnyLodge == \E p \in Posts : Lodge(p)

Next ==
  \/ AnyRead
  \/ AnyReread
  \/ AnyLodge
  \/ ApplyHead
  \/ Rest

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_centreVars
  /\ WF_centreVars(AnyRead)
  /\ WF_centreVars(AnyReread)
  /\ WF_centreVars(ApplyHead)
  /\ SF_centreVars(AnyLodge)

\* No lost update: the rewrites waiting in the queue form a contiguous version
\* chain anchored at the board's current stamp, so each one will be applied to
\* exactly the board version its author read, never on top of a rewrite it
\* never saw.
QueueIsAContiguousChain ==
  \A i \in 1 .. Len(queue) : queue[i].base = stamp + i - 1

EveryPostGetsWritten ==
  \A p \in Posts : (posture[p] = "lodged") ~> (posture[p] = "written")
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    NumPosts = 3
    QueueCap = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT QueueIsAContiguousChain

PROPERTY EveryPostGetsWritten
nl:
A subway signalling centre keeps one shared occupancy board. Each trackside signal post owns one field of that board and needs to rewrite it once during the shift. Posts do not touch the board directly; they lodge their rewrites in a bounded hand-off queue that the centre drains in order. The queue is the only path to the board and it applies back pressure: once it holds as many rewrites as it is sized for, nothing more may be lodged until the centre has drained some. Posts are slow but never failed -- a post may sit on a step for an arbitrarily long time, but it always eventually takes it.

The board carries a version stamp that advances by one every time the centre applies a rewrite. Before lodging, a post reads the queue's tail version, which is the board stamp plus however many rewrites are already waiting -- that is, the version its own rewrite would land on. If another post lodges in the meantime, the reading a post is holding is no longer the tail, and rather than lodging blind it takes a fresh reading. A post may only lodge its rewrite while the version it is holding is still the tail and the queue is below its cap; the rewrite is stamped with that version as its base.

The centre drains the queue from the head: it takes the oldest waiting rewrite, applies it to the board field of its author, advances the board stamp by one, and marks that post as written. When every post has been written the centre rests.

The full action set is: take a fresh reading of the queue's tail version from a quiet post, re-read the tail version when the held reading has gone stale, lodge a rewrite while the held reading is still the tail and the queue is below its cap, apply the rewrite at the head of the queue to the board and advance the stamp, and rest once every post has been written.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The rewrites waiting in the hand-off queue always form one unbroken version chain anchored at the board's current stamp -- the first waiting rewrite is based on the current stamp, the second on the one after it, and so on -- so every rewrite is applied to exactly the board version its author read and no update is ever laid down on top of a change its author never saw.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every rewrite lodged in the hand-off queue is eventually applied to the shared board.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od9m1p1t3 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS NumFeeders, Slots

Feeders == 0 .. (NumFeeders - 1)
Blank == "blank"
Hold == "hold"

\* The shed order book is one shared record: a fixed strip of numbered slots
\* plus a cursor saying which slot is next. A feeder reads the cursor to work
\* out which slot its own order will land in, and writes into that slot later.
\* The baton circulating round the ring is what keeps the reading it took from
\* going stale under it before the write lands.

VARIABLES baton, standing, penciled, cursor, orderBook
gridVars == <<baton, standing, penciled, cursor, orderBook>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ baton \in Feeders
  /\ standing \in [Feeders -> {"idle", "drafting", "filed", "passed"}]
  /\ penciled \in [Feeders -> 0 .. Slots]
  /\ cursor \in 0 .. Slots
  /\ orderBook \in [1 .. Slots -> Feeders \cup {Blank, Hold}]

Init ==
  /\ baton = 0
  /\ standing = [f \in Feeders |-> "idle"]
  /\ penciled = [f \in Feeders |-> 0]
  /\ cursor = 0
  /\ orderBook = [i \in 1 .. Slots |-> Blank]

\* The baton moves on only when its holder is not mid-draft; a slow feeder may
\* sit on it for as long as it likes, but it is never skipped over.
PassBaton ==
  /\ standing[baton] # "drafting"
  /\ baton' = (baton + 1) % NumFeeders
  /\ UNCHANGED <<standing, penciled, cursor, orderBook>>

\* Read half of the read-modify-write: pencil in which slot this order will use.
TakeReading(f) ==
  /\ baton = f
  /\ standing[f] = "idle"
  /\ cursor < Slots
  /\ penciled' = [penciled EXCEPT ![f] = cursor + 1]
  /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![f] = "drafting"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, cursor, orderBook>>

\* Write half: the shed order lands in the pencilled slot and the cursor moves.
FileOrder(f) ==
  /\ baton = f
  /\ standing[f] = "drafting"
  /\ orderBook' = [orderBook EXCEPT ![penciled[f]] = f]
  /\ cursor' = penciled[f]
  /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![f] = "filed"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, penciled>>

\* The feeder decides no shedding is needed and burns its slot with a hold mark.
LodgeHold(f) ==
  /\ baton = f
  /\ standing[f] = "drafting"
  /\ orderBook' = [orderBook EXCEPT ![penciled[f]] = Hold]
  /\ cursor' = penciled[f]
  /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![f] = "passed"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, penciled>>

\* Late telemetry: the feeder drops the draft and gives its reading back.
DropDraft(f) ==
  /\ baton = f
  /\ standing[f] = "drafting"
  /\ penciled' = [penciled EXCEPT ![f] = 0]
  /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![f] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, cursor, orderBook>>

Next ==
  \/ PassBaton
  \/ \E f \in Feeders : TakeReading(f)
  \/ \E f \in Feeders : FileOrder(f)
  \/ \E f \in Feeders : LodgeHold(f)
  \/ \E f \in Feeders : DropDraft(f)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_gridVars

\* No lost update: a feeder that has filed still finds its own name in the slot
\* it pencilled, so nobody's shed order was quietly written over by a feeder
\* that had read the same cursor value.
FiledOrdersStayOwn ==
  \A f \in Feeders : standing[f] = "filed" => orderBook[penciled[f]] = f
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    NumFeeders = 3
    Slots = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT FiledOrdersStayOwn
nl:
A regional power grid runs an automatic load shedder. The feeders that can be shed are wired into a ring, and they all write into one shared record: the shed order book, which is a strip of numbered slots plus a cursor saying which slot the next order will occupy. A baton circulates around the ring, and only the feeder currently holding the baton may work on the order book.

Filing an order is a read followed by a write, with a gap in between. First the feeder reads the cursor and pencils in the slot number its own order is going to use. Later it performs the write, stamping its name into the pencilled slot and moving the cursor forward to that slot. The gap between reading the cursor and writing the slot is exactly where an order could be lost: if two feeders both read the same cursor value, they would both pencil the same slot and the second write would quietly erase the first feeder's order. The baton closes that gap, because the baton only moves on when its holder is not in the middle of a draft.

Feeders here are slow but never failed. A feeder may sit on the baton for an arbitrarily long time before doing anything, and it is never skipped over or forced off, but it always eventually acts. A feeder that has pencilled a slot has three ways to finish: it can file a real shed order into that slot, it can decide no shedding is needed and burn the slot with a hold mark instead, or, if its telemetry arrives too late to be useful, it can drop the draft entirely and give the pencilled reading back without touching the order book.

The full action set is: pass the baton on to the next feeder in the ring when its holder is not mid-draft, take a reading of the cursor and pencil in the next slot, file a shed order into the pencilled slot and advance the cursor, lodge a hold mark into the pencilled slot and advance the cursor, and drop a draft and give the pencilled reading back.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every feeder that has filed a shed order still finds its own name in the slot it pencilled, so no feeder's update to the shared order book is ever silently overwritten by another feeder that had read the same cursor value.

spec_text:
----------------------------- MODULE W4Od19m9p3t0 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Branches, Tickets, NumBays, MaxEpoch

Bays == 1 .. NumBays
Empty == "empty"

\* Hold-bay ownership is re-cut every configuration epoch. A branch may only
\* fill a bay it owns in the epoch it has caught up to, so a branch that has
\* gone silent simply stops filling and its bays are re-cut to a live branch.

VARIABLES epoch, owns, alive, bayTag, register, caughtUp
libVars == <<epoch, owns, alive, bayTag, register, caughtUp>>

Placed(t) == \E a \in register : a.ticket = t
LiveBranches == {b \in Branches : alive[b]}

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 1 .. MaxEpoch
  /\ owns \in [Bays -> Branches]
  /\ alive \in [Branches -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ bayTag \in [Bays -> Tickets \cup {Empty}]
  /\ caughtUp \in [Branches -> 0 .. MaxEpoch]

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 1
  /\ owns = [y \in Bays |-> CHOOSE b \in Branches : TRUE]
  /\ alive = [b \in Branches |-> TRUE]
  /\ bayTag = [y \in Bays |-> Empty]
  /\ register = {}
  /\ caughtUp = [b \in Branches |-> 0]

\* Re-cut: a fresh epoch hands every bay to some branch believed to be running.
Recut ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ \E f \in [Bays -> LiveBranches] : owns' = f
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, bayTag, register, caughtUp>>

\* A branch goes quiet without telling anyone. At most one ever does, and never
\* after the last re-cut, so a live branch can always be handed the bays.
GoSilent(b) ==
  /\ alive[b]
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ \A c \in Branches : c # b => alive[c]
  /\ alive' = [alive EXCEPT ![b] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owns, bayTag, register, caughtUp>>

CatchUp(b) ==
  /\ alive[b]
  /\ caughtUp[b] < epoch
  /\ caughtUp' = [caughtUp EXCEPT ![b] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owns, alive, bayTag, register>>

\* Filling a bay tags the shelf and writes the desk's register entry together.
FillBay(b, t, y) ==
  /\ alive[b]
  /\ caughtUp[b] = epoch
  /\ owns[y] = b
  /\ bayTag[y] = Empty
  /\ ~Placed(t)
  /\ bayTag' = [bayTag EXCEPT ![y] = t]
  /\ register' = register \cup {[ticket |-> t, bay |-> y, ep |-> epoch]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, owns, alive, caughtUp>>

AnyCatchUp == \E b \in Branches : CatchUp(b)
AnyFill == \E b \in Branches, t \in Tickets, y \in Bays : FillBay(b, t, y)

Settled == epoch = MaxEpoch /\ UNCHANGED libVars

Next ==
  \/ Recut
  \/ \E b \in Branches : GoSilent(b)
  \/ AnyCatchUp
  \/ AnyFill
  \/ Settled

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_libVars
  /\ WF_libVars(Recut)
  /\ WF_libVars(AnyCatchUp)
  /\ WF_libVars(AnyFill)

\* No bay is handed out twice: every entry in the desk register still finds its
\* own ticket on the physical shelf tag of the bay it names. A bay given to a
\* second reservation would overwrite the tag and strand the earlier entry.
RegisterMatchesTheShelf ==
  \A a \in register : bayTag[a.bay] = a.ticket

EveryTicketFindsABay ==
  \A t \in Tickets : (~Placed(t)) ~> Placed(t)
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Branches = {northside, riverbank}
    Tickets = {hold1, hold2}
    NumBays = 2
    MaxEpoch = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT RegisterMatchesTheShelf

PROPERTY EveryTicketFindsABay
nl:
A city library system holds reserved books on a bank of numbered hold bays behind the front desk. Several branch systems share the bank, and which branch is responsible for which bay is not fixed: the bay assignment is re-cut from time to time, and each re-cut opens a new numbered configuration epoch. A branch may only fill a bay if it owns that bay and has caught up to the current epoch, so a branch running on an old epoch's assignment does nothing at all.

One branch can go silent. It does not announce anything and it does not fail loudly; it simply stops taking part, and nothing distinguishes a silent branch from a slow one except that it never acts again. At most one branch ever goes silent, and never after the final re-cut, so the re-cut that follows can always hand the bays to a branch that is still running.

Filling a bay for a waiting reservation ticket does two things in one step: it puts the physical shelf tag with the ticket's name on the bay, and it writes an entry into the front desk's register recording which ticket went into which bay and in which epoch. A branch will only fill a bay whose shelf tag is currently empty, and only for a ticket that has no register entry yet. Once the final epoch has been reached and no more re-cuts are possible, the system settles.

The full action set is: re-cut the bay assignment into a new epoch, handing every bay to a branch believed to be running; let a branch go silent; let a running branch catch up to the current epoch; fill an empty owned bay for an unplaced ticket, tagging the shelf and writing the register entry together; and settle once the final epoch is reached.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every entry in the front desk register still finds its own ticket on the physical shelf tag of the bay that entry names, so a bay is never handed out to a second reservation -- which would overwrite the tag and strand the earlier register entry -- however the epochs are re-cut.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every reservation ticket eventually gets a hold bay, even if the branch that originally owned the bays has gone silent.

spec_text:
------------------------------ MODULE W4Od9m2p3t5 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Feeders, Dispatchers, NumWindows

Windows == 1 .. NumWindows
Unlet == "unlet"
NoPick == 0

\* Each shed window may be let to at most one feeder. A feeder wins a window
\* only by getting every dispatcher to sign off on it, and it keeps a local
\* list of the windows it believes are its own. The control room can overrule
\* the whole vote, but a re-let must strike the window off the old holder's
\* list in the same breath.

VARIABLES letting, believes, mode, pick, signoffs
shedVars == <<letting, believes, mode, pick, signoffs>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ letting \in [Windows -> Feeders \cup {Unlet}]
  /\ believes \in [Feeders -> SUBSET Windows]
  /\ mode \in [Feeders -> {"quiet", "polling"}]
  /\ pick \in [Feeders -> Windows \cup {NoPick}]
  /\ signoffs \in [Feeders -> SUBSET Dispatchers]

Init ==
  /\ letting = [w \in Windows |-> Unlet]
  /\ believes = [f \in Feeders |-> {}]
  /\ mode = [f \in Feeders |-> "quiet"]
  /\ pick = [f \in Feeders |-> NoPick]
  /\ signoffs = [f \in Feeders |-> {}]

OpenPoll(f, w) ==
  /\ mode[f] = "quiet"
  /\ letting[w] = Unlet
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![f] = "polling"]
  /\ pick' = [pick EXCEPT ![f] = w]
  /\ signoffs' = [signoffs EXCEPT ![f] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<letting, believes>>

SignOff(f, d) ==
  /\ mode[f] = "polling"
  /\ d \notin signoffs[f]
  /\ letting[pick[f]] = Unlet
  /\ signoffs' = [signoffs EXCEPT ![f] = signoffs[f] \cup {d}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<letting, believes, mode, pick>>

\* Unanimity closes the deal: the window is let and joins the feeder's list.
SealPoll(f) ==
  /\ mode[f] = "polling"
  /\ signoffs[f] = Dispatchers
  /\ letting[pick[f]] = Unlet
  /\ letting' = [letting EXCEPT ![pick[f]] = f]
  /\ believes' = [believes EXCEPT ![f] = believes[f] \cup {pick[f]}]
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![f] = "quiet"]
  /\ pick' = [pick EXCEPT ![f] = NoPick]
  /\ UNCHANGED signoffs

DropPoll(f) ==
  /\ mode[f] = "polling"
  /\ letting[pick[f]] # Unlet
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![f] = "quiet"]
  /\ pick' = [pick EXCEPT ![f] = NoPick]
  /\ signoffs' = [signoffs EXCEPT ![f] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<letting, believes>>

\* Privileged override: the control room re-lets a window to whoever it wants,
\* vote or no vote, striking it off every other feeder's list as it does so.
ControlRoomRelet(w, f) ==
  /\ letting' = [letting EXCEPT ![w] = f]
  /\ believes' = [g \in Feeders |->
       IF g = f THEN believes[g] \cup {w} ELSE believes[g] \ {w}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<mode, pick, signoffs>>

HandBack(f, w) ==
  /\ mode[f] = "quiet"
  /\ w \in believes[f]
  /\ letting' = [letting EXCEPT ![w] = Unlet]
  /\ believes' = [believes EXCEPT ![f] = believes[f] \ {w}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<mode, pick, signoffs>>

Next ==
  \/ \E f \in Feeders, w \in Windows : OpenPoll(f, w)
  \/ \E f \in Feeders, d \in Dispatchers : SignOff(f, d)
  \/ \E f \in Feeders : SealPoll(f)
  \/ \E f \in Feeders : DropPoll(f)
  \/ \E w \in Windows, f \in Feeders : ControlRoomRelet(w, f)
  \/ \E f \in Feeders, w \in Windows : HandBack(f, w)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_shedVars

\* No window is let twice over: whatever a feeder believes is its own is inside
\* the set of windows the regional letting actually records against that feeder,
\* so two feeders can never both be counting on the same window.
BeliefsSitInsideTheLetting ==
  \A f \in Feeders :
    believes[f] \subseteq {w \in Windows : letting[w] = f}
================================================================================
nl:
A regional power grid sheds load in numbered shed windows. Each window may be let to at most one feeder at a time, and the region keeps an authoritative letting record saying which feeder, if any, currently has each window. Separately, every feeder keeps its own local list of the windows it believes are its own to shed in, and that local list is what the feeder actually acts on.

Winning a window is a two-phase commit across the regional dispatchers. A quiet feeder opens a poll by naming an unlet window; every dispatcher then signs off on that poll individually, and a dispatcher will only sign off while the named window is still unlet. When the whole set of dispatchers has signed off and the window is still unlet, the feeder seals the poll: the letting record is written in that feeder's name, the window joins that feeder's local list, and the feeder goes quiet again. If the named window has been let out from under the poll before it can be sealed, the feeder drops the poll and goes quiet with nothing gained.

The control room has a privileged override. It may re-let any window to any feeder at any moment, with no poll and no dispatcher sign-off at all. When it does, it strikes that window off every other feeder's local list in the same breath as it adds the window to the new holder's list, so the override never leaves two feeders counting on one window. Finally, a quiet feeder may hand a window back, clearing the letting record and dropping the window from its own list.

The full action set is: open a poll on an unlet window, sign off on an open poll as one dispatcher, seal a unanimously signed-off poll and take the window, drop a poll whose window has been let elsewhere, re-let a window by control room override while striking it off every other feeder's list, and hand a held window back.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whatever windows a feeder believes are its own always sit inside the set of windows the regional letting record actually holds in that feeder's name, so no shed window is ever allocated to two feeders at once, not even by the control room override.

----------------------------- MODULE W4Od17m4p5t4 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Bags, MaxLanes

\* Sending a bag down the one-way loading chute is irreversible: past the flap
\* it is on the aircraft and cannot be recalled. The hand-off belt in front of
\* the flap is bounded and pushes back when full, and the number of lanes the
\* belt runs on is retuned by the ramp supervisor while the flight is loading.

VARIABLES lanes, belt, stage, manifest
routerVars == <<lanes, belt, stage, manifest>>

OnManifest(b) == \E i \in 1 .. Len(manifest) : manifest[i] = b
BeltFull == Len(belt) >= lanes

TypeOK ==
  /\ lanes \in 1 .. MaxLanes
  /\ stage \in [Bags -> {"arrived", "screened", "onbelt", "loaded"}]

Init ==
  /\ lanes = 1
  /\ belt = <<>>
  /\ stage = [b \in Bags |-> "arrived"]
  /\ manifest = <<>>

\* The supervisor opens another lane on the hand-off belt.
WidenBelt ==
  /\ lanes < MaxLanes
  /\ lanes' = lanes + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<belt, stage, manifest>>

\* And closes one again -- never below what is already standing on the belt.
NarrowBelt ==
  /\ lanes > 1
  /\ lanes - 1 >= Len(belt)
  /\ lanes' = lanes - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<belt, stage, manifest>>

ReadTag(b) ==
  /\ stage[b] = "arrived"
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![b] = "screened"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lanes, belt, manifest>>

\* Back pressure: a screened bag waits off-belt while the belt is at its lanes.
StepOnBelt(b) ==
  /\ stage[b] = "screened"
  /\ ~BeltFull
  /\ belt' = Append(belt, b)
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![b] = "onbelt"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lanes, manifest>>

\* The irreversible step, taken on the bag at the head of the belt only.
DropThroughFlap ==
  /\ Len(belt) > 0
  /\ manifest' = Append(manifest, Head(belt))
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![Head(belt)] = "loaded"]
  /\ belt' = Tail(belt)
  /\ UNCHANGED lanes

AnyRead == \E b \in Bags : ReadTag(b)
AnyStepOn == \E b \in Bags : StepOnBelt(b)

Next ==
  \/ WidenBelt
  \/ NarrowBelt
  \/ AnyRead
  \/ AnyStepOn
  \/ DropThroughFlap

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_routerVars
  /\ WF_routerVars(AnyRead)
  /\ WF_routerVars(DropThroughFlap)
  /\ SF_routerVars(AnyStepOn)

\* Nothing standing on the hand-off belt is already written on the aircraft's
\* load manifest. A bag that went through the flap twice would be on the
\* manifest while a second copy of it was still queued behind the flap.
NothingOnBeltIsAlreadyAboard ==
  \A i \in 1 .. Len(belt) : ~OnManifest(belt[i])

EveryBagIsLoaded ==
  \A b \in Bags : (stage[b] # "loaded") ~> (stage[b] = "loaded")
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Bags = {tagA, tagB, tagC}
    MaxLanes = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NothingOnBeltIsAlreadyAboard

PROPERTY EveryBagIsLoaded
nl:
An airport baggage router feeds one aircraft. Bags arrive at the router, get their tags read, and then wait for a place on the hand-off belt that runs up to the loading flap. Dropping a bag through the flap is irreversible: past the flap the bag is in the aircraft hold and cannot be recalled, and every drop is written as a line on the flight's load manifest.

The hand-off belt is bounded, and it applies back pressure: a screened bag may only step onto the belt while the belt is holding fewer bags than it has lanes running, otherwise the bag simply waits off-belt. The number of lanes is not fixed for the flight. The ramp supervisor retunes it while loading is in progress -- opening another lane to let more bags queue up, or closing one again, though never closing the belt down below the number of bags already standing on it.

Bags are dropped through the flap strictly from the head of the belt, one at a time, and the bag that goes through leaves the belt as it does so. A bag's tag is read once, it steps onto the belt once, and it goes through the flap once.

The full action set is: open another lane on the hand-off belt, close a lane while the belt is short enough to allow it, read an arrived bag's tag, step a screened bag onto the belt while the belt is below its lane count, and drop the bag at the head of the belt through the loading flap onto the manifest.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No bag standing on the hand-off belt is already written on the aircraft's load manifest, so a bag can never go through the loading flap a second time while a duplicate of it is still queued behind the flap.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every bag that arrives at the router is eventually dropped through the flap and written onto the load manifest, however the supervisor retunes the belt's lanes.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od9m7p3t3 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Substations, NumRotaSlots, MaxTurnovers

RotaSlots == 1 .. NumRotaSlots
Vacant == "vacant"
NoAim == 0

\* Each rota slot is one compare-and-swap cell holding the substation on duty
\* plus a turnover count. A substation primes by reading the turnover count,
\* then swaps itself in only if the cell is still vacant at that same count.
\* Substations are slow, never dead: the gap between priming and swapping can
\* be arbitrarily long, which is exactly what the turnover count guards.

VARIABLES onDuty, turnovers, posture, aim, primedAt
rotaVars == <<onDuty, turnovers, posture, aim, primedAt>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ onDuty \in [RotaSlots -> Substations \cup {Vacant}]
  /\ turnovers \in [RotaSlots -> 0 .. MaxTurnovers]
  /\ posture \in [Substations -> {"off", "primed", "onrota"}]
  /\ aim \in [Substations -> RotaSlots \cup {NoAim}]
  /\ primedAt \in [Substations -> 0 .. MaxTurnovers]

Init ==
  /\ onDuty = [k \in RotaSlots |-> Vacant]
  /\ turnovers = [k \in RotaSlots |-> 0]
  /\ posture = [s \in Substations |-> "off"]
  /\ aim = [s \in Substations |-> NoAim]
  /\ primedAt = [s \in Substations |-> 0]

\* Read half of the compare-and-swap.
Prime(s, k) ==
  /\ posture[s] = "off"
  /\ posture' = [posture EXCEPT ![s] = "primed"]
  /\ aim' = [aim EXCEPT ![s] = k]
  /\ primedAt' = [primedAt EXCEPT ![s] = turnovers[k]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<onDuty, turnovers>>

\* A slow substation whose reading has aged can simply take a newer one.
Refresh(s) ==
  /\ posture[s] = "primed"
  /\ primedAt[s] # turnovers[aim[s]]
  /\ primedAt' = [primedAt EXCEPT ![s] = turnovers[aim[s]]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<onDuty, turnovers, posture, aim>>

\* Swap half: it lands only against a vacant cell at the very count that was
\* read, and it bumps that count so every other outstanding reading ages out.
SwapIn(s) ==
  /\ posture[s] = "primed"
  /\ onDuty[aim[s]] = Vacant
  /\ turnovers[aim[s]] = primedAt[s]
  /\ turnovers[aim[s]] < MaxTurnovers
  /\ onDuty' = [onDuty EXCEPT ![aim[s]] = s]
  /\ turnovers' = [turnovers EXCEPT ![aim[s]] = turnovers[aim[s]] + 1]
  /\ primedAt' = [primedAt EXCEPT ![s] = turnovers[aim[s]] + 1]
  /\ posture' = [posture EXCEPT ![s] = "onrota"]
  /\ UNCHANGED aim

GiveUp(s) ==
  /\ posture[s] = "primed"
  /\ posture' = [posture EXCEPT ![s] = "off"]
  /\ aim' = [aim EXCEPT ![s] = NoAim]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<onDuty, turnovers, primedAt>>

StandDown(s) ==
  /\ posture[s] = "onrota"
  /\ onDuty' = [onDuty EXCEPT ![aim[s]] = Vacant]
  /\ posture' = [posture EXCEPT ![s] = "off"]
  /\ aim' = [aim EXCEPT ![s] = NoAim]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<turnovers, primedAt>>

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in Substations, k \in RotaSlots : Prime(s, k)
  \/ \E s \in Substations : Refresh(s)
  \/ \E s \in Substations : SwapIn(s)
  \/ \E s \in Substations : GiveUp(s)
  \/ \E s \in Substations : StandDown(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_rotaVars

\* Nobody stands on a rota slot at a stale turnover count. A slot handed to a
\* second substation would bump its count past what the first one swapped at,
\* so this failing is exactly the signature of a doubly allocated slot.
DutyReadingsStayCurrent ==
  \A s \in Substations :
    posture[s] = "onrota" => turnovers[aim[s]] = primedAt[s]
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Substations = {millrace, quarryhead}
    NumRotaSlots = 2
    MaxTurnovers = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT DutyReadingsStayCurrent
nl:
A power-grid load shedder runs a curtailment rota with a small number of numbered duty slots. Each duty slot is held in a single compare-and-swap cell that stores two things: which substation is currently on duty in that slot, or that the slot is vacant, and a turnover count that goes up by one every time the slot is taken. A slot must never be allocated to two substations at once.

A substation takes a slot in two steps with a gap between them. First it primes: it names the slot it wants and reads that slot's turnover count into its own working note. Later it attempts the swap. The swap lands only if the slot is still vacant and its turnover count is still exactly the number written on the working note; landing writes the substation into the cell and bumps the turnover count, which is what ages out every other outstanding reading of that slot. The substation's own note is updated to the new count as part of the same swap.

Substations here are slow, not failed. An arbitrarily long time may pass between priming and swapping, and that is precisely the window the turnover count is there to guard. A substation whose note has aged may simply refresh it against the slot's current count and try again, or it may give up on the attempt entirely and go back to being off the rota. A substation that is on the rota may later stand down, vacating its slot without touching the turnover count. Slots stop accepting new duty once their turnover count reaches its ceiling.

The full action set is: prime against a named slot by reading its turnover count, refresh a working note that has aged, swap into a vacant slot whose turnover count still matches the note and bump that count, give up on a primed attempt, and stand down from a slot held on the rota.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No substation on the rota is standing on a slot whose turnover count has moved past the count it swapped at, so a slot handed to a second substation -- which would bump the count past the first one's -- can never happen.

----------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m3p1t4 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Centres, MaxTerm, MaxHeadway

NoDraft == [at |-> 0, want |-> 0]
NoLeader == "noleader"
Headways == 1 .. MaxHeadway

\* The shared record is the line's headway setting -- how tightly trains may be
\* packed through the blocks -- together with the term it was last written in.
\* Only the centre elected in the live term may draft a change, and a failover
\* bumps the term and tears up every draft, so a draft written from a term that
\* has already been superseded can never land on top of a newer one.

VARIABLES term, chief, draft, headway, headwayTerm, enforced
lineVars == <<term, chief, draft, headway, headwayTerm, enforced>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ term \in 0 .. MaxTerm
  /\ chief \in Centres \cup {NoLeader}
  /\ draft \in [Centres -> {NoDraft} \cup [at : 1 .. MaxTerm, want : Headways]]
  /\ headway \in Headways
  /\ headwayTerm \in 0 .. MaxTerm
  /\ enforced \in [Centres -> Headways]

Init ==
  /\ term = 0
  /\ chief = NoLeader
  /\ draft = [c \in Centres |-> NoDraft]
  /\ headway = 1
  /\ headwayTerm = 0
  /\ enforced = [c \in Centres |-> 1]

\* Failover: a new term, a new chief, and every outstanding draft torn up.
Failover(c) ==
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ chief' = c
  /\ draft' = [d \in Centres |-> NoDraft]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<headway, headwayTerm, enforced>>

\* Only the chief of the live term drafts, and it stamps the live term on it.
Compose(c, h) ==
  /\ chief = c
  /\ draft[c] = NoDraft
  /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![c] = [at |-> term, want |-> h]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, chief, headway, headwayTerm, enforced>>

\* The draft lands on the shared record and carries its term across with it.
Commit(c) ==
  /\ draft[c] # NoDraft
  /\ draft[c].at >= headwayTerm
  /\ headway' = draft[c].want
  /\ headwayTerm' = draft[c].at
  /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![c] = NoDraft]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, chief, enforced>>

Withdraw(c) ==
  /\ draft[c] # NoDraft
  /\ draft' = [draft EXCEPT ![c] = NoDraft]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, chief, headway, headwayTerm, enforced>>

\* Every centre eventually runs its blocks at whatever the record now says.
Adopt(c) ==
  /\ enforced[c] # headway
  /\ enforced' = [enforced EXCEPT ![c] = headway]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, chief, draft, headway, headwayTerm>>

AnyCommit == \E c \in Centres : Commit(c)

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Centres : Failover(c)
  \/ \E c \in Centres, h \in Headways : Compose(c, h)
  \/ AnyCommit
  \/ \E c \in Centres : Withdraw(c)
  \/ \E c \in Centres : Adopt(c)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_lineVars
  /\ WF_lineVars(AnyCommit)

\* No lost update: nothing anywhere in the system is holding a draft stamped
\* with a superseded term, so no write can land on top of a headway change made
\* by a later chief that the drafter never saw.
NoDraftFromADeadTerm ==
  \A c \in Centres : draft[c] # NoDraft => draft[c].at = term

EveryDraftSettles ==
  \A c \in Centres : (draft[c] # NoDraft) ~> (draft[c] = NoDraft)
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Centres = {kingsway, dockgate}
    MaxTerm = 2
    MaxHeadway = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoDraftFromADeadTerm

PROPERTY EveryDraftSettles
nl:
A subway line's block signalling is run from a set of interchangeable signalling centres. They share one record that matters: the line's headway setting, which says how tightly trains may be packed through the blocks, together with the term number in which that setting was last written. The headway is not a fixed design parameter; it is retuned at runtime as service patterns change, which is exactly why the record has to survive concurrent editing.

The centres run leader election with failover. A failover opens a new, higher term and installs one centre as chief for that term. Only the chief of the live term may draft a change to the headway, and the draft it composes carries the live term stamped on it. The crucial part of failover is that opening a new term also tears up every draft that was outstanding, so a centre that was chief a moment ago is left holding nothing at all.

A draft lands on the shared record by being committed: the headway takes the drafted value and the record's term takes the draft's term, and the draft is cleared. A chief may also simply withdraw a draft it no longer wants, clearing it without writing anything. Separately, each centre eventually starts running its own blocks at whatever headway the shared record currently states.

The full action set is: fail over to a new term with a named chief and tear up every outstanding draft, compose a draft headway as chief of the live term, commit a draft onto the shared record and carry its term across, withdraw a draft without writing it, and adopt the record's current headway at one centre.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No centre anywhere in the system is holding a draft stamped with a term that has already been superseded, so a write can never land on top of a headway change made by a later chief that the drafting centre never saw.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every draft a chief composes is eventually settled, either committed onto the shared record or cleared away.
