------------------------------ MODULE W4Od2m8p2t4 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS NumBots, NumRacks, StartPerRack, MaxRackCap

Bots == 1 .. NumBots
Racks == 1 .. NumRacks
NoRack == 0
TotalTotes == NumRacks * StartPerRack

\* Two lock levels, taken coarse-first and given back fine-first: a bot must
\* hold the floor lock before it may pin a rack, and must unpin the rack before
\* it lets the floor lock go. Totes are only ever moved between a pinned rack
\* and the bot's own claw, so the tote count on the floor never changes.

RECURSIVE SumTo(_, _)
SumTo(f, n) == IF n = 0 THEN 0 ELSE f[n] + SumTo(f, n - 1)

VARIABLES floorLock, rackPin, pinnedBy, claw, onRack, rackCap
yardVars == <<floorLock, rackPin, pinnedBy, claw, onRack, rackCap>>

Free == 0

TypeOK ==
  /\ floorLock \in Bots \cup {Free}
  /\ rackPin \in [Racks -> Bots \cup {Free}]
  /\ pinnedBy \in [Bots -> Racks \cup {NoRack}]
  /\ claw \in [Bots -> 0 .. 1]
  /\ onRack \in [Racks -> 0 .. MaxRackCap]
  /\ rackCap \in 1 .. MaxRackCap

Init ==
  /\ floorLock = Free
  /\ rackPin = [r \in Racks |-> Free]
  /\ pinnedBy = [b \in Bots |-> NoRack]
  /\ claw = [b \in Bots |-> 0]
  /\ onRack = [r \in Racks |-> StartPerRack]
  /\ rackCap = StartPerRack

\* The floor supervisor retunes how deep a rack may be stacked, but never
\* below what is already sitting on the racks.
RetuneRackCap ==
  /\ \E n \in 1 .. MaxRackCap :
       /\ n # rackCap
       /\ \A r \in Racks : onRack[r] =< n
       /\ rackCap' = n
  /\ UNCHANGED <<floorLock, rackPin, pinnedBy, claw, onRack>>

TakeFloor(b) ==
  /\ floorLock = Free
  /\ floorLock' = b
  /\ UNCHANGED <<rackPin, pinnedBy, claw, onRack, rackCap>>

PinRack(b, r) ==
  /\ floorLock = b
  /\ pinnedBy[b] = NoRack
  /\ rackPin[r] = Free
  /\ rackPin' = [rackPin EXCEPT ![r] = b]
  /\ pinnedBy' = [pinnedBy EXCEPT ![b] = r]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<floorLock, claw, onRack, rackCap>>

\* A tote leaves the rack and sits in the claw; nothing is created here.
Lift(b) ==
  /\ pinnedBy[b] # NoRack
  /\ claw[b] = 0
  /\ onRack[pinnedBy[b]] > 0
  /\ onRack' = [onRack EXCEPT ![pinnedBy[b]] = onRack[pinnedBy[b]] - 1]
  /\ claw' = [claw EXCEPT ![b] = 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<floorLock, rackPin, pinnedBy, rackCap>>

\* And back the other way, subject to whatever the rack depth is set to now.
Stow(b) ==
  /\ pinnedBy[b] # NoRack
  /\ claw[b] = 1
  /\ onRack[pinnedBy[b]] < rackCap
  /\ onRack' = [onRack EXCEPT ![pinnedBy[b]] = onRack[pinnedBy[b]] + 1]
  /\ claw' = [claw EXCEPT ![b] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<floorLock, rackPin, pinnedBy, rackCap>>

Unpin(b) ==
  /\ pinnedBy[b] # NoRack
  /\ rackPin' = [rackPin EXCEPT ![pinnedBy[b]] = Free]
  /\ pinnedBy' = [pinnedBy EXCEPT ![b] = NoRack]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<floorLock, claw, onRack, rackCap>>

DropFloor(b) ==
  /\ floorLock = b
  /\ pinnedBy[b] = NoRack
  /\ floorLock' = Free
  /\ UNCHANGED <<rackPin, pinnedBy, claw, onRack, rackCap>>

Next ==
  \/ RetuneRackCap
  \/ \E b \in Bots : TakeFloor(b)
  \/ \E b \in Bots, r \in Racks : PinRack(b, r)
  \/ \E b \in Bots : Lift(b)
  \/ \E b \in Bots : Stow(b)
  \/ \E b \in Bots : Unpin(b)
  \/ \E b \in Bots : DropFloor(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_yardVars

\* Totes on racks plus totes in claws always come to the number the shift
\* started with: no lift, stow, pin, unpin or retune makes or loses a tote.
TotesAreConserved ==
  SumTo(onRack, NumRacks) + SumTo(claw, NumBots) = TotalTotes
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    NumBots = 2
    NumRacks = 2
    StartPerRack = 1
    MaxRackCap = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT TotesAreConserved
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet shuttles totes between numbered storage racks on one floor. Every tote on that floor at the start of the shift stays on the floor: totes are only ever moved between a rack and a robot's claw, never brought in and never taken away.

Access to the racks goes through two lock levels, taken coarse first and given back fine first. A robot must hold the single floor lock before it may pin any rack, and it may pin only one rack at a time. Having pinned a rack, the robot may lift a tote off it into its claw, or stow the tote in its claw onto the rack. A robot may unpin its rack whether or not it is carrying a tote -- carrying one across the floor is normal -- and only once it has unpinned may it let go of the floor lock, which is what lets the next robot in.

Rack depth is not a fixed number. The floor supervisor retunes at runtime how deep a rack may be stacked, and a stow is refused when the target rack already holds as many totes as the current setting allows. The supervisor never sets the depth below what is already sitting on the racks, so retuning never has to spill anything.

The full action set is: retune the rack depth setting, take the floor lock, pin a free rack while holding the floor lock, lift a tote off the pinned rack into the claw, stow the tote from the claw onto the pinned rack while there is depth for it, unpin the pinned rack, and let go of the floor lock once no rack is pinned.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The totes sitting on the racks plus the totes riding in robot claws always add up to exactly the number of totes the floor started the shift with, so no lift, stow, pin, unpin or depth retune ever creates or destroys a tote.

spec_text:
----------------------------- MODULE W4Od14m4p6t5 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Drones, Sorties, QueueCap, MaxIssue

Grounded == "grounded"

\* A drone may only work a sortie on a badge issued in the live issue number,
\* or under the incident commander's standing waiver. Re-issuing the badges
\* grounds every unwaived drone in the same step and throws its sortie back on
\* the board, so nothing is ever flown on a stale credential.

VARIABLES issue, badge, waiver, board, flying, sortieState
swarmVars == <<issue, badge, waiver, board, flying, sortieState>>

Cleared(d) == badge[d] = issue \/ d \in waiver

TypeOK ==
  /\ issue \in 0 .. MaxIssue
  /\ badge \in [Drones -> 0 .. MaxIssue]
  /\ waiver \subseteq Drones
  /\ flying \in [Drones -> Sorties \cup {Grounded}]
  /\ sortieState \in [Sorties -> {"filed", "boarded", "aloft", "flown"}]

Init ==
  /\ issue = 0
  /\ badge = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
  /\ waiver = {}
  /\ board = <<>>
  /\ flying = [d \in Drones |-> Grounded]
  /\ sortieState = [s \in Sorties |-> "filed"]

\* Re-issue: every badge below the new issue number goes dead at once, and any
\* drone flying on one is grounded with its sortie put back on the board.
Reissue ==
  /\ issue < MaxIssue
  /\ issue' = issue + 1
  /\ LET pulled == {flying[d] : d \in Drones \ waiver} \ {Grounded}
     IN /\ flying' = [d \in Drones |->
             IF d \in waiver THEN flying[d] ELSE Grounded]
        /\ sortieState' = [s \in Sorties |->
             IF s \in pulled THEN "filed" ELSE sortieState[s]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<badge, waiver, board>>

Rebadge(d) ==
  /\ badge[d] < issue
  /\ badge' = [badge EXCEPT ![d] = issue]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<issue, waiver, board, flying, sortieState>>

\* Privileged override: the incident commander waives the badge rule outright.
CommanderWaiver(d) ==
  /\ d \notin waiver
  /\ waiver' = waiver \cup {d}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<issue, badge, board, flying, sortieState>>

\* Back pressure: the tasking board is bounded and refuses new work when full.
PostSortie(s) ==
  /\ sortieState[s] = "filed"
  /\ Len(board) < QueueCap
  /\ board' = Append(board, s)
  /\ sortieState' = [sortieState EXCEPT ![s] = "boarded"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<issue, badge, waiver, flying>>

Launch(d) ==
  /\ flying[d] = Grounded
  /\ Cleared(d)
  /\ Len(board) > 0
  /\ flying' = [flying EXCEPT ![d] = Head(board)]
  /\ sortieState' = [sortieState EXCEPT ![Head(board)] = "aloft"]
  /\ board' = Tail(board)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<issue, badge, waiver>>

Survey(d) ==
  /\ flying[d] # Grounded
  /\ Cleared(d)
  /\ sortieState' = [sortieState EXCEPT ![flying[d]] = "flown"]
  /\ flying' = [flying EXCEPT ![d] = Grounded]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<issue, badge, waiver, board>>

AnyPost == \E s \in Sorties : PostSortie(s)
AnyLaunch == \E d \in Drones : Launch(d)
AnySurvey == \E d \in Drones : Survey(d)
AnyRebadge == \E d \in Drones : Rebadge(d)

Standby == (\A s \in Sorties : sortieState[s] = "flown") /\ UNCHANGED swarmVars

Next ==
  \/ Reissue
  \/ AnyRebadge
  \/ \E d \in Drones : CommanderWaiver(d)
  \/ AnyPost
  \/ AnyLaunch
  \/ AnySurvey
  \/ Standby

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_swarmVars
  /\ WF_swarmVars(AnyRebadge)
  /\ WF_swarmVars(AnySurvey)
  /\ SF_swarmVars(AnyPost)
  /\ SF_swarmVars(AnyLaunch)

\* Nothing is in the air on a dead credential: every drone carrying a sortie is
\* either badged at the live issue number or covered by the commander's waiver.
NothingFliesOnADeadBadge ==
  \A d \in Drones : flying[d] # Grounded => Cleared(d)

EverySortieGetsFlown ==
  \A s \in Sorties : (sortieState[s] # "flown") ~> (sortieState[s] = "flown")
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Drones = {kite, hawk}
    Sorties = {ridgeline, canyon}
    QueueCap = 2
    MaxIssue = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NothingFliesOnADeadBadge

PROPERTY EverySortieGetsFlown
nl:
A wildfire surveillance swarm flies numbered survey sorties over a fire front. Sorties are handed out through a tasking board, which is a bounded work queue: a filed sortie may only be posted onto the board while the board is holding fewer sorties than it is sized for, so the board pushes back when it is full. Drones take the sortie at the head of the board, fly it, and report it flown.

Flying authority is controlled by badge issue numbers. The operations cell publishes an issue number, and a drone's badge is only good while it matches the live issue number. Re-issuing the badges is a single step that raises the live issue number, which instantly kills every badge below it; in the same step every drone that was flying on a now-dead badge is grounded and the sortie it was carrying goes straight back to being filed, ready to be posted again. A grounded drone renews its badge to the live issue number and is then cleared again.

There is one privileged exception. The incident commander may grant a standing waiver to a named drone. A waived drone counts as cleared regardless of what its badge says, is not grounded by a re-issue, and keeps the sortie it is carrying across the re-issue. Waivers are only ever granted, never withdrawn.

A drone may only launch onto a sortie, and may only report a sortie flown, while it is cleared -- badged at the live issue number, or waived. Once every sortie has been flown the swarm sits on standby.

The full action set is: re-issue the badges, grounding unwaived drones and returning their sorties to filed; renew one drone's badge to the live issue number; grant the commander's standing waiver to a drone; post a filed sortie onto the board while the board is below its cap; launch a cleared, grounded drone onto the sortie at the head of the board; report a sortie flown by the cleared drone carrying it; and sit on standby once everything is flown.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No drone is ever in the air carrying a sortie on a dead credential -- every drone holding a sortie is either badged at the live issue number or covered by the commander's standing waiver.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every filed sortie is eventually flown, however many times the badges are re-issued and drones are grounded mid-flight.

----------------------------- MODULE W4Od15m0p4t0 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Brokers, NumRungs, RungCap

Rungs == 1 .. NumRungs

\* Pre-open orders are lodged optimistically: a broker reads the book stamp,
\* and its lodgement only lands if the stamp has not moved underneath it. A
\* rung's allowance is charged against parked orders and resting orders
\* together, so crossing a parked order into the book frees nothing.

VARIABLES stamp, posture, rung, stampSeen, resting, parked
auctionVars == <<stamp, posture, rung, stampSeen, resting, parked>>

Taken(k) == resting[k] + parked[k]

TypeOK ==
  /\ stamp \in 0 .. NumRungs
  /\ posture \in [Brokers -> {"clear", "armed", "lodged", "dark"}]
  /\ rung \in [Brokers -> Rungs]
  /\ stampSeen \in [Brokers -> 0 .. NumRungs]
  /\ resting \in [Rungs -> 0 .. RungCap]
  /\ parked \in [Rungs -> 0 .. RungCap]

Init ==
  /\ stamp = 0
  /\ posture = [b \in Brokers |-> "clear"]
  /\ rung = [b \in Brokers |-> 1]
  /\ stampSeen = [b \in Brokers |-> 0]
  /\ resting = [k \in Rungs |-> 0]
  /\ parked = [k \in Rungs |-> 0]

Peek(b, k) ==
  /\ posture[b] = "clear"
  /\ posture' = [posture EXCEPT ![b] = "armed"]
  /\ rung' = [rung EXCEPT ![b] = k]
  /\ stampSeen' = [stampSeen EXCEPT ![b] = stamp]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stamp, resting, parked>>

\* Retry: the attempt is doomed, either because the stamp moved or because the
\* rung filled up, so the broker re-aims and takes a fresh reading.
Retry(b, k) ==
  /\ posture[b] = "armed"
  /\ \/ stampSeen[b] # stamp
     \/ Taken(rung[b]) >= RungCap
  /\ rung' = [rung EXCEPT ![b] = k]
  /\ stampSeen' = [stampSeen EXCEPT ![b] = stamp]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stamp, posture, resting, parked>>

\* The lodgement lands only against the stamp the broker read, and only into
\* whatever allowance the rung has left.
Lodge(b) ==
  /\ posture[b] = "armed"
  /\ stampSeen[b] = stamp
  /\ Taken(rung[b]) < RungCap
  /\ parked' = [parked EXCEPT ![rung[b]] = parked[rung[b]] + 1]
  /\ stamp' = stamp + 1
  /\ posture' = [posture EXCEPT ![b] = "lodged"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<rung, stampSeen, resting>>

\* The cross moves a parked order onto the book; the rung's allowance is
\* unchanged by this, because it was already charged at lodgement time.
Cross(k) ==
  /\ parked[k] > 0
  /\ parked' = [parked EXCEPT ![k] = parked[k] - 1]
  /\ resting' = [resting EXCEPT ![k] = resting[k] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stamp, posture, rung, stampSeen>>

\* One broker's link can drop without a word; it simply never acts again.
GoDark(b) ==
  /\ posture[b] \in {"clear", "armed"}
  /\ \A c \in Brokers : posture[c] # "dark"
  /\ posture' = [posture EXCEPT ![b] = "dark"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stamp, rung, stampSeen, resting, parked>>

Halt ==
  /\ \A b \in Brokers : posture[b] \in {"lodged", "dark"}
  /\ \A k \in Rungs : parked[k] = 0
  /\ UNCHANGED auctionVars

Next ==
  \/ \E b \in Brokers, k \in Rungs : Peek(b, k)
  \/ \E b \in Brokers, k \in Rungs : Retry(b, k)
  \/ \E b \in Brokers : Lodge(b)
  \/ \E k \in Rungs : Cross(k)
  \/ \E b \in Brokers : GoDark(b)
  \/ Halt

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_auctionVars

\* No price rung is ever oversubscribed: the orders resting on a rung plus the
\* orders parked against it never together exceed that rung's allowance, even
\* though brokers race each other with optimistic lodgements.
RungAllowanceHolds ==
  \A k \in Rungs : resting[k] + parked[k] <= RungCap
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Brokers = {alphacap, beacon, cormorant}
    NumRungs = 2
    RungCap = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT RungAllowanceHolds
nl:
A stock exchange runs an opening auction. Orders are lodged against numbered price rungs before the cross, and each rung has a strict allowance: only so many orders may be associated with a rung at once. The allowance is charged against parked orders and resting orders together, so an order that is parked against a rung is already eating that rung's allowance before the cross ever happens.

Brokers lodge optimistically rather than taking any kind of lock. A clear broker peeks at the book: it aims at a rung and copies the book's current stamp into its own note. It may then lodge, but the lodgement only lands if the stamp on its note is still the book's live stamp and the rung it is aiming at still has allowance left. A landed lodgement parks one order against that rung and bumps the book stamp, which is what invalidates every other broker's note. A broker whose attempt is doomed -- because the stamp moved under it, or because the rung it aimed at has filled up -- retries: it re-aims at a rung, possibly a different one, and takes a fresh reading of the stamp.

Separately, the cross moves parked orders onto the book: one parked order against a rung becomes one resting order on that rung. This does not change how much of the rung's allowance is used, since the order was charged at lodgement time.

One broker's link can drop without warning. There is no error message and no timeout visible to anyone; the broker simply never takes another step, and at most one broker in the auction ever goes dark this way. Once every broker has either lodged or gone dark and nothing is left parked, the auction halts.

The full action set is: peek at the book by aiming at a rung and copying the stamp, retry a doomed attempt by re-aiming and re-reading the stamp, lodge an order against the aimed rung while the stamp still matches and the rung has allowance, cross one parked order on a rung into a resting order, let one broker go dark, and halt once everything is lodged or dark and nothing is parked.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No price rung is ever oversubscribed -- the orders resting on a rung plus the orders parked against it never together exceed that rung's allowance, even though brokers race each other with optimistic lodgements and one of them may drop out silently mid-attempt.

----------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m0p2t1 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Machines, StockAtDepot

Crates == [to : Machines]

\* Every can lives in exactly one of three places: the depot shelf, a crate on
\* the road, or a machine's hopper. Crates travel over a courier network that
\* delivers in whatever order it likes, so the depot ledger stamp -- not the
\* order of traffic -- is what decides whether a draw request is still good.

VARIABLES shelf, hopper, road, ledgerStamp, stampNoted, routine
netVars == <<shelf, hopper, road, ledgerStamp, stampNoted, routine>>

RECURSIVE HopperTotal(_)
HopperTotal(S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET m == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE
       IN hopper[m] + HopperTotal(S \ {m})

MaxDraws == Cardinality(Machines)

TypeOK ==
  /\ shelf \in 0 .. StockAtDepot
  /\ hopper \in [Machines -> 0 .. StockAtDepot]
  /\ road \subseteq Crates
  /\ ledgerStamp \in 0 .. MaxDraws
  /\ stampNoted \in [Machines -> 0 .. MaxDraws]
  /\ routine \in [Machines -> {"quiet", "quoted", "enroute", "stocked"}]

Init ==
  /\ shelf = StockAtDepot
  /\ hopper = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
  /\ road = {}
  /\ ledgerStamp = 0
  /\ stampNoted = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
  /\ routine = [m \in Machines |-> "quiet"]

QuoteStock(m) ==
  /\ routine[m] = "quiet"
  /\ stampNoted' = [stampNoted EXCEPT ![m] = ledgerStamp]
  /\ routine' = [routine EXCEPT ![m] = "quoted"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, hopper, road, ledgerStamp>>

\* Somebody else drew first, so the noted stamp is worthless; note it again.
Requote(m) ==
  /\ routine[m] = "quoted"
  /\ stampNoted[m] # ledgerStamp
  /\ stampNoted' = [stampNoted EXCEPT ![m] = ledgerStamp]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, hopper, road, ledgerStamp, routine>>

\* The draw lands only against the stamp that was noted. One can leaves the
\* shelf and becomes exactly one crate on the road -- nothing is minted here.
DrawCrate(m) ==
  /\ routine[m] = "quoted"
  /\ stampNoted[m] = ledgerStamp
  /\ shelf > 0
  /\ shelf' = shelf - 1
  /\ road' = road \cup {[to |-> m]}
  /\ ledgerStamp' = ledgerStamp + 1
  /\ routine' = [routine EXCEPT ![m] = "enroute"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<hopper, stampNoted>>

\* The courier drops crates in any order it pleases.
DropOff(c) ==
  /\ c \in road
  /\ road' = road \ {c}
  /\ hopper' = [hopper EXCEPT ![c.to] = hopper[c.to] + 1]
  /\ routine' = [routine EXCEPT ![c.to] = "stocked"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, ledgerStamp, stampNoted>>

AnyQuote == \E m \in Machines : QuoteStock(m)
AnyRequote == \E m \in Machines : Requote(m)
AnyDraw == \E m \in Machines : DrawCrate(m)
AnyDrop == \E c \in Crates : DropOff(c)

RouteClear == (\A m \in Machines : routine[m] = "stocked") /\ UNCHANGED netVars

Next ==
  \/ AnyQuote
  \/ AnyRequote
  \/ AnyDraw
  \/ AnyDrop
  \/ RouteClear

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_netVars
  /\ WF_netVars(AnyQuote)
  /\ WF_netVars(AnyRequote)
  /\ WF_netVars(AnyDrop)
  /\ SF_netVars(AnyDraw)

\* Cans on the depot shelf, cans riding on the road, and cans in the machines'
\* hoppers always add back up to the stock the depot opened with.
CansAreConserved ==
  shelf + Cardinality(road) + HopperTotal(Machines) = StockAtDepot

EveryMachineGetsStocked ==
  \A m \in Machines : (routine[m] # "stocked") ~> (routine[m] = "stocked")
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Machines = {atrium, platform}
    StockAtDepot = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT CansAreConserved

PROPERTY EveryMachineGetsStocked
nl:
A vending machine network is restocked from one depot. Every can in the network is in exactly one of three places: on the depot shelf, riding in a crate on the road, or sitting in a machine's hopper. Nothing is bought in and nothing is thrown away during the restock round.

The depot's stock ledger carries a stamp that goes up by one every time a can is drawn off the shelf. Machines do not lock the ledger; they work optimistically. A quiet machine quotes the stock, which means noting the ledger's current stamp on its own docket. It may then draw a crate, but the draw only lands if the stamp on its docket is still the ledger's live stamp and the shelf is not empty. A machine that finds another machine drew first simply notes the stamp again and tries afresh.

A landed draw takes one can off the shelf and turns it into exactly one crate on the road, and bumps the ledger stamp. Crates travel by courier, and the courier delivers in whatever order it likes -- a crate posted later may well arrive first, and a crate may sit on the road for an arbitrarily long time. Dropping a crate off moves its can out of the crate and into the destination machine's hopper, and that machine is then stocked. Once every machine is stocked the round is over and the route is clear.

The full action set is: quote the stock by noting the ledger stamp, re-quote when the noted stamp has been overtaken, draw a crate off the shelf while the noted stamp still matches and bump the ledger stamp, drop a crate off into its destination machine's hopper, and stand down once the route is clear.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The cans on the depot shelf, the cans riding in crates on the road, and the cans sitting in machine hoppers always add back up to exactly the stock the depot opened the round with, so no can is created or destroyed by a draw, a delivery, or a losing optimistic retry.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every machine in the network eventually gets its crate delivered into its hopper, however the courier reorders the road and however often a machine loses the race for the ledger stamp.

----------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m1p3t5 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS NumCabins, NumBerths, Units, LogBook

Cabins == 0 .. (NumCabins - 1)
Berths == 1 .. NumBerths
Vacant == "vacant"
Stabled == 0
DutyDesk == "dutydesk"

\* Berth allocations are written in one shared log book. A baton goes round the
\* signal cabins and only the cabin holding it may write a line, except for the
\* duty desk, which writes whenever it likes. The log book itself is the record
\* that must stay sane: readings of one berth must alternate take, give, take.

VARIABLES baton, sittingIn, berthOf, logbook
terminusVars == <<baton, sittingIn, berthOf, logbook>>

RECURSIVE StillOpen(_, _)
StillOpen(b, k) ==
  IF k = 0 THEN FALSE
  ELSE IF logbook[k].berth = b
       THEN logbook[k].kind = "take"
       ELSE StillOpen(b, k - 1)

Room == Len(logbook) < LogBook

TypeOK ==
  /\ baton \in Cabins
  /\ sittingIn \in [Berths -> Units \cup {Vacant}]
  /\ berthOf \in [Units -> Berths \cup {Stabled}]

Init ==
  /\ baton = 0
  /\ sittingIn = [b \in Berths |-> Vacant]
  /\ berthOf = [u \in Units |-> Stabled]
  /\ logbook = <<>>

PassBaton ==
  /\ baton' = (baton + 1) % NumCabins
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sittingIn, berthOf, logbook>>

\* Only the baton-holding cabin may allocate, and only into a vacant berth.
TakeBerth(c, u, b) ==
  /\ baton = c
  /\ Room
  /\ sittingIn[b] = Vacant
  /\ berthOf[u] = Stabled
  /\ sittingIn' = [sittingIn EXCEPT ![b] = u]
  /\ berthOf' = [berthOf EXCEPT ![u] = b]
  /\ logbook' = Append(logbook, [berth |-> b, kind |-> "take", by |-> c])
  /\ UNCHANGED baton

GiveBerth(c, b) ==
  /\ baton = c
  /\ Room
  /\ sittingIn[b] # Vacant
  /\ berthOf' = [berthOf EXCEPT ![sittingIn[b]] = Stabled]
  /\ sittingIn' = [sittingIn EXCEPT ![b] = Vacant]
  /\ logbook' = Append(logbook, [berth |-> b, kind |-> "give", by |-> c])
  /\ UNCHANGED baton

\* Privileged override: the duty desk allocates without holding the baton at
\* all, but it still reads the berth first and still writes its line.
DutyTake(u, b) ==
  /\ Room
  /\ sittingIn[b] = Vacant
  /\ berthOf[u] = Stabled
  /\ sittingIn' = [sittingIn EXCEPT ![b] = u]
  /\ berthOf' = [berthOf EXCEPT ![u] = b]
  /\ logbook' = Append(logbook, [berth |-> b, kind |-> "take", by |-> DutyDesk])
  /\ UNCHANGED baton

DutyGive(b) ==
  /\ Room
  /\ sittingIn[b] # Vacant
  /\ berthOf' = [berthOf EXCEPT ![sittingIn[b]] = Stabled]
  /\ sittingIn' = [sittingIn EXCEPT ![b] = Vacant]
  /\ logbook' = Append(logbook, [berth |-> b, kind |-> "give", by |-> DutyDesk])
  /\ UNCHANGED baton

Next ==
  \/ PassBaton
  \/ \E c \in Cabins, u \in Units, b \in Berths : TakeBerth(c, u, b)
  \/ \E c \in Cabins, b \in Berths : GiveBerth(c, b)
  \/ \E u \in Units, b \in Berths : DutyTake(u, b)
  \/ \E b \in Berths : DutyGive(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_terminusVars

\* No berth is allocated twice over: reading the log book from the top, no
\* take line for a berth is written while that berth's last line was itself a
\* take, whether the line came from a cabin or from the duty desk.
NoTakeOverAnOpenBerth ==
  \A i \in 1 .. Len(logbook) :
    logbook[i].kind = "take" => ~StillOpen(logbook[i].berth, i - 1)
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    NumCabins = 2
    NumBerths = 2
    Units = {setA, setB}
    LogBook = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT NoTakeOverAnOpenBerth
nl:
A subway terminus has a small number of numbered berths where train sets stand between runs. Allocations are made by signal cabins, and every allocation and release is written as a line in one shared log book with a limited number of pages: which berth, whether it was a take or a give, and who wrote it. A berth must never be allocated to a second train set while it is still allocated to the first.

The cabins pass a baton around a ring, and only the cabin currently holding the baton may write a line into the log book. Taking a berth requires that the berth is standing vacant and that the train set being berthed is currently stabled; the take marks the berth as holding that set, records the set's berth, and writes a take line. Giving a berth back releases whichever set is sitting there, marks the berth vacant again, and writes a give line.

The duty desk has a privileged override. It may take or give a berth at any time without holding the baton at all. What it does not skip is the read: it still checks that a berth is vacant before taking it, and it still writes its line into the same log book under its own name, so the book stays the single record of what happened.

The full action set is: pass the baton to the next cabin in the ring, take a vacant berth for a stabled train set as the baton-holding cabin, give a berth back as the baton-holding cabin, take a vacant berth for a stabled train set from the duty desk without the baton, and give a berth back from the duty desk without the baton.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Reading the log book from the top, no take line for a berth is ever written at a point where that berth's most recent line was itself a take, so a berth is never allocated to a second train set while the first is still in it -- whether the line came from a cabin holding the baton or from the duty desk overriding it.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od4m2p3t3 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Cars, Stages, NumCradles

Cradles == 1 .. NumCradles
Nobody == "nobody"
NoPick == 0

\* Each wash stage keeps its own copy of which cradle is spoken for. A car is
\* only put on the line once every stage has written the same car against the
\* same cradle, so the stages can never end up disagreeing about a cradle.
\* Stages are slow, never dead: they answer late, but they always answer.

VARIABLES spokenFor, standing, wants, agreed
lineVars == <<spokenFor, standing, wants, agreed>>

SomebodyBidding == \E c \in Cars : standing[c] = "bidding"

TypeOK ==
  /\ spokenFor \in [Stages -> [Cradles -> Cars \cup {Nobody}]]
  /\ standing \in [Cars -> {"waiting", "bidding", "online", "done"}]
  /\ wants \in [Cars -> Cradles \cup {NoPick}]
  /\ agreed \in [Cars -> SUBSET Stages]

Init ==
  /\ spokenFor = [g \in Stages |-> [k \in Cradles |-> Nobody]]
  /\ standing = [c \in Cars |-> "waiting"]
  /\ wants = [c \in Cars |-> NoPick]
  /\ agreed = [c \in Cars |-> {}]

\* Only one car sits at the bidding gate at a time; that is the conveyor.
OpenBid(c, k) ==
  /\ standing[c] = "waiting"
  /\ ~SomebodyBidding
  /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![c] = "bidding"]
  /\ wants' = [wants EXCEPT ![c] = k]
  /\ agreed' = [agreed EXCEPT ![c] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED spokenFor

\* One stage writes the bidding car against the cradle in its own copy.
StageAgrees(c, g) ==
  /\ standing[c] = "bidding"
  /\ g \notin agreed[c]
  /\ spokenFor[g][wants[c]] = Nobody
  /\ spokenFor' = [spokenFor EXCEPT ![g][wants[c]] = c]
  /\ agreed' = [agreed EXCEPT ![c] = agreed[c] \cup {g}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<standing, wants>>

\* Unanimity puts the car on the line.
Commit(c) ==
  /\ standing[c] = "bidding"
  /\ agreed[c] = Stages
  /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![c] = "online"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<spokenFor, wants, agreed>>

\* Some stage has the cradle down to somebody else, so the bid is unwound and
\* every copy this car had already written is scrubbed out again.
RollBack(c) ==
  /\ standing[c] = "bidding"
  /\ \E g \in Stages : g \notin agreed[c] /\ spokenFor[g][wants[c]] # Nobody
  /\ spokenFor' = [g \in Stages |->
       [k \in Cradles |->
          IF k = wants[c] /\ spokenFor[g][k] = c THEN Nobody
          ELSE spokenFor[g][k]]]
  /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![c] = "waiting"]
  /\ wants' = [wants EXCEPT ![c] = NoPick]
  /\ agreed' = [agreed EXCEPT ![c] = {}]

RollOff(c) ==
  /\ standing[c] = "online"
  /\ spokenFor' = [g \in Stages |->
       [k \in Cradles |->
          IF spokenFor[g][k] = c THEN Nobody ELSE spokenFor[g][k]]]
  /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![c] = "done"]
  /\ wants' = [wants EXCEPT ![c] = NoPick]
  /\ agreed' = [agreed EXCEPT ![c] = {}]

AnyAgree == \E c \in Cars, g \in Stages : StageAgrees(c, g)
AnyCommit == \E c \in Cars : Commit(c)
AnyRollBack == \E c \in Cars : RollBack(c)

Shut == (\A c \in Cars : standing[c] = "done") /\ UNCHANGED lineVars

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Cars, k \in Cradles : OpenBid(c, k)
  \/ AnyAgree
  \/ AnyCommit
  \/ AnyRollBack
  \/ \E c \in Cars : RollOff(c)
  \/ Shut

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_lineVars
  /\ WF_lineVars(AnyAgree)
  /\ WF_lineVars(AnyCommit)
  /\ WF_lineVars(AnyRollBack)

\* No cradle is allocated twice: two stages never have the same cradle written
\* down against two different cars.
StagesNeverDisagree ==
  \A k \in Cradles : \A p, q \in Stages :
    (spokenFor[p][k] # Nobody /\ spokenFor[q][k] # Nobody)
      => spokenFor[p][k] = spokenFor[q][k]

EveryBidResolves ==
  \A c \in Cars : (standing[c] = "bidding") ~> (standing[c] # "bidding")
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Cars = {estate, coupe}
    Stages = {prewash, dryer}
    NumCradles = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT StagesNeverDisagree

PROPERTY EveryBidResolves
nl:
An automatic car wash runs vehicles along a conveyor on numbered cradles. Several wash stages -- prewash, dryer, and so on -- each keep their own copy of which cradle is spoken for and by which car. A cradle must never end up allocated to two different cars, which here means no two stages may have the same cradle written down against different cars.

Getting a car onto the line is a two-phase commit across the stages. Only one car sits at the bidding gate at a time, which is what the conveyor enforces. The car at the gate opens a bid by naming a cradle. Each stage in turn writes that car against that cradle in its own copy, but a stage will only do so if its copy shows the cradle free. Stages here are slow but never failed: a stage may take an arbitrarily long time to answer a bid, but it always answers in the end.

When every stage has written the car against the cradle, the bid commits and the car goes onto the line. If instead some stage that has not yet answered shows the cradle already spoken for by somebody else, the bid is rolled back: every copy this car had already been written into is scrubbed out again, and the car goes back to waiting, free to bid later for whatever cradle it likes. A car that has been on the line eventually rolls off at the end, and rolling off scrubs that car out of every stage's copy, freeing its cradle. Once every car is done the wash shuts down.

The full action set is: open a bid on a named cradle from the one car at the gate, have one stage write the bidding car against the cradle in its own copy, commit a bid that every stage has written, roll a bid back and scrub out the copies it had already been written into, roll a finished car off the line and scrub it out of every stage's copy, and shut down once every car is done.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No two wash stages ever have the same cradle written down against two different cars, so a cradle is never allocated twice over even while a bid is only part way through the stages.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every bid opened at the gate is eventually resolved -- either committed onto the line or rolled back -- so no car is left bidding forever.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od0m7p1t0 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Planners, Theatres, MaxRevisions

Unbooked == "unbooked"

\* The day plan is one compare-and-swap register: a revision number plus the
\* theatre roster. A planner reads the revision number, and its swap only
\* lands while that number is still live. Every landed swap is written into
\* the plan's revision chain, recording the revision it was built on.

VARIABLES revision, chain, posture, noted, roster
planVars == <<revision, chain, posture, noted, roster>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ revision \in 0 .. MaxRevisions
  /\ posture \in [Planners -> {"clear", "staged", "silent"}]
  /\ noted \in [Planners -> 0 .. MaxRevisions]
  /\ roster \in [Theatres -> Planners \cup {Unbooked}]

Init ==
  /\ revision = 0
  /\ chain = <<>>
  /\ posture = [p \in Planners |-> "clear"]
  /\ noted = [p \in Planners |-> 0]
  /\ roster = [h \in Theatres |-> Unbooked]

ReadPlan(p) ==
  /\ posture[p] = "clear"
  /\ noted' = [noted EXCEPT ![p] = revision]
  /\ posture' = [posture EXCEPT ![p] = "staged"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<revision, chain, roster>>

\* Somebody swapped first, so the note the planner is holding has aged out.
Refresh(p) ==
  /\ posture[p] = "staged"
  /\ noted[p] # revision
  /\ noted' = [noted EXCEPT ![p] = revision]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<revision, chain, posture, roster>>

\* Swap half: it lands only against the revision that was read, and the chain
\* line it writes records exactly which revision it was built on.
SwapIn(p, h) ==
  /\ posture[p] = "staged"
  /\ noted[p] = revision
  /\ revision < MaxRevisions
  /\ roster' = [roster EXCEPT ![h] = p]
  /\ revision' = revision + 1
  /\ chain' = Append(chain,
       [built |-> noted[p], made |-> revision + 1, room |-> h, by |-> p])
  /\ posture' = [posture EXCEPT ![p] = "clear"]
  /\ UNCHANGED noted

\* One planner's terminal can drop off the network without any notice at all.
FallSilent(p) ==
  /\ posture[p] \in {"clear", "staged"}
  /\ \A q \in Planners : posture[q] # "silent"
  /\ posture' = [posture EXCEPT ![p] = "silent"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<revision, chain, noted, roster>>

Adjourn == revision = MaxRevisions /\ UNCHANGED planVars

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Planners : ReadPlan(p)
  \/ \E p \in Planners : Refresh(p)
  \/ \E p \in Planners, h \in Theatres : SwapIn(p, h)
  \/ \E p \in Planners : FallSilent(p)
  \/ Adjourn

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_planVars

\* No lost update: the revision chain is unbroken. Every line was built on the
\* revision the line before it produced, so no planner's booking was ever laid
\* down over a colleague's booking that the planner had not read.
ChainIsUnbroken ==
  \A i \in 1 .. Len(chain) :
    chain[i].built = (IF i = 1 THEN 0 ELSE chain[i - 1].made)
================================================================================
nl:
A hospital's operating-room scheduler keeps the whole day plan in one shared register: a revision number together with the theatre roster saying which planner has booked each theatre. Several planners work on the plan at once, and none of them locks it. Instead they use a compare-and-swap discipline.

A clear planner reads the plan, noting the current revision number on its own working slip. Later it attempts to swap in a booking for a theatre. The swap lands only if the revision number on its slip is still the register's live revision; if a colleague swapped in first, the slip has aged out and the planner must refresh it against the live revision before trying again. A landed swap writes the planner into the roster for the chosen theatre, raises the revision number by one, and appends a line to the plan's revision chain recording which revision the booking was built on, which revision it produced, which theatre it touched, and who made it. Bookings stop once the revision number reaches its ceiling for the day.

One planner's terminal can drop off the network with no notice whatever. There is no alarm, no timeout, and nothing anybody else can see; that planner simply never takes another step. At most one planner in the department goes silent this way. When the revision ceiling is reached the department adjourns.

The full action set is: read the plan and note the live revision on a slip, refresh a slip that has aged out, swap in a theatre booking while the noted revision is still live, let one planner fall silent, and adjourn once the revision ceiling is reached.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The plan's revision chain is unbroken -- every line in it was built on exactly the revision that the line before it produced -- so no planner's booking was ever laid down on top of a colleague's booking that the planner had not read.

------------------------------ MODULE W4Od7m3p6t0 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Gantries, Lifts, MaxTerm

Slack == "slack"
NoChief == "nochief"

\* Only the gantry that holds the yard chief seat, and holds it on the term the
\* yard is actually running, may have a box off the ground. Electing a new
\* chief opens a new term and slackens every other gantry's spreader, which is
\* what stops a gantry that has gone quiet from still counting as authorised.

VARIABLES yardTerm, chief, believes, spreader, lift, quiet
craneVars == <<yardTerm, chief, believes, spreader, lift, quiet>>

Authorised(g) == chief = g /\ believes[g] = yardTerm

TypeOK ==
  /\ yardTerm \in 0 .. MaxTerm
  /\ chief \in Gantries \cup {NoChief}
  /\ believes \in [Gantries -> 0 .. MaxTerm]
  /\ spreader \in [Gantries -> Lifts \cup {Slack}]
  /\ lift \in [Lifts -> {"grounded", "airborne", "stowed"}]
  /\ quiet \subseteq Gantries

Init ==
  /\ yardTerm = 0
  /\ chief = NoChief
  /\ believes = [g \in Gantries |-> 0]
  /\ spreader = [g \in Gantries |-> Slack]
  /\ lift = [b \in Lifts |-> "grounded"]
  /\ quiet = {}

\* A new term, a new chief, and every other spreader slackened; any box that
\* was in the air under an old chief comes back to the ground.
Elect(g) ==
  /\ yardTerm < MaxTerm
  /\ g \notin quiet
  /\ yardTerm' = yardTerm + 1
  /\ chief' = g
  /\ believes' = [believes EXCEPT ![g] = yardTerm + 1]
  /\ spreader' = [d \in Gantries |-> IF d = g THEN spreader[d] ELSE Slack]
  /\ lift' = [b \in Lifts |->
       IF \E d \in Gantries : d # g /\ spreader[d] = b
       THEN "grounded" ELSE lift[b]]
  /\ UNCHANGED quiet

Hoist(g, b) ==
  /\ Authorised(g)
  /\ g \notin quiet
  /\ spreader[g] = Slack
  /\ lift[b] = "grounded"
  /\ spreader' = [spreader EXCEPT ![g] = b]
  /\ lift' = [lift EXCEPT ![b] = "airborne"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<yardTerm, chief, believes, quiet>>

Stow(g) ==
  /\ Authorised(g)
  /\ g \notin quiet
  /\ spreader[g] # Slack
  /\ lift' = [lift EXCEPT ![spreader[g]] = "stowed"]
  /\ spreader' = [spreader EXCEPT ![g] = Slack]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<yardTerm, chief, believes, quiet>>

\* One gantry's cab radio can die without a word; it never acts again.
GoQuiet(g) ==
  /\ quiet = {}
  /\ yardTerm < MaxTerm
  /\ quiet' = {g}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<yardTerm, chief, believes, spreader, lift>>

AnyElect == \E g \in Gantries : Elect(g)
AnyHoist == \E g \in Gantries, b \in Lifts : Hoist(g, b)
AnyStow == \E g \in Gantries : Stow(g)

Idle == yardTerm = MaxTerm /\ UNCHANGED craneVars

Next ==
  \/ AnyElect
  \/ AnyHoist
  \/ AnyStow
  \/ \E g \in Gantries : GoQuiet(g)
  \/ Idle

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_craneVars
  /\ WF_craneVars(AnyElect)
  /\ WF_craneVars(AnyHoist)
  /\ WF_craneVars(AnyStow)

\* Nothing is off the ground except under live authority: any gantry with a box
\* on its spreader is the yard chief and holds the seat on the running term.
OnlyTheLiveChiefLifts ==
  \A g \in Gantries : spreader[g] # Slack => Authorised(g)

EveryBoxGetsStowed ==
  \A b \in Lifts : (lift[b] # "stowed") ~> (lift[b] = "stowed")
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Gantries = {quayA, quayB}
    Lifts = {boxRed, boxBlue}
    MaxTerm = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT OnlyTheLiveChiefLifts

PROPERTY EveryBoxGetsStowed
nl:
A container-ship crane yard is worked by several rail-mounted gantries. Only one gantry at a time holds the yard chief seat, and the yard runs in numbered terms. A gantry counts as authorised only if it is the chief and it believes it holds the seat on the term the yard is actually running; a gantry still believing in an older term is stale and counts for nothing, no matter what it thinks.

Electing a chief opens a new term. The newly elected gantry is told the new term number in the same step. Electing also slackens every other gantry's spreader, and any box that was in the air under a previous chief is set back down on the ground, so the yard never carries authority forward across a failover.

Only an authorised gantry may hoist a grounded box onto its spreader, and only an authorised gantry may stow the box it is carrying. One gantry's cab radio can die without a word: no alarm, no message, nothing anyone can observe except that the gantry never acts again. At most one gantry in the yard goes quiet like this, and never after the yard's final term has been opened, so there is always a further election available to hand the seat to a gantry that is still working. Once the final term has been opened the yard runs on until everything is stowed and then idles.

The full action set is: elect a working gantry as chief on a new term, slackening every other spreader and grounding whatever they were carrying; hoist a grounded box onto an authorised gantry's spreader; stow the box an authorised gantry is carrying; let one gantry go quiet without notice; and idle once the final term has been opened.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Nothing is ever off the ground except under live authority -- any gantry with a box on its spreader is the yard chief and holds that seat on the term the yard is currently running.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every box in the yard is eventually stowed, even if the gantry holding it goes quiet mid-lift and the seat has to be handed on.

----------------------------- MODULE W4Od12m1p2t1 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Units, NumFridges

Fridges == 0 .. (NumFridges - 1)
Crates == [unit : Units, from : Fridges]

\* Every unit of blood sits in exactly one of four places: cold store, a crate
\* on the courier run, quarantine awaiting crossmatch, or issued. The courier
\* run is a bag, not a line: crates come off it in whatever order they like.
\* A rota baton says which fridge may touch the cold store this turn.

VARIABLES baton, coldStore, courierRun, quarantine, issued
bankVars == <<baton, coldStore, courierRun, quarantine, issued>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ baton \in Fridges
  /\ coldStore \subseteq Units
  /\ courierRun \subseteq Crates
  /\ quarantine \subseteq Units
  /\ issued \subseteq Units

Init ==
  /\ baton = 0
  /\ coldStore = Units
  /\ courierRun = {}
  /\ quarantine = {}
  /\ issued = {}

PassBaton ==
  /\ baton' = (baton + 1) % NumFridges
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coldStore, courierRun, quarantine, issued>>

\* A unit leaves the cold store and becomes exactly one crate on the run.
CrateUp(f, u) ==
  /\ baton = f
  /\ u \in coldStore
  /\ coldStore' = coldStore \ {u}
  /\ courierRun' = courierRun \cup {[unit |-> u, from |-> f]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, quarantine, issued>>

\* Any crate on the run may be the next one taken off it; the courier keeps no
\* order at all. Its unit lands in quarantine, still one unit, still whole.
TakeOff(c) ==
  /\ c \in courierRun
  /\ courierRun' = courierRun \ {c}
  /\ quarantine' = quarantine \cup {c.unit}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, coldStore, issued>>

Crossmatch(f, u) ==
  /\ baton = f
  /\ u \in quarantine
  /\ quarantine' = quarantine \ {u}
  /\ coldStore' = coldStore \cup {u}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, courierRun, issued>>

IssueUnit(f, u) ==
  /\ baton = f
  /\ u \in coldStore
  /\ coldStore' = coldStore \ {u}
  /\ issued' = issued \cup {u}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, courierRun, quarantine>>

Next ==
  \/ PassBaton
  \/ \E f \in Fridges, u \in Units : CrateUp(f, u)
  \/ \E c \in Crates : TakeOff(c)
  \/ \E f \in Fridges, u \in Units : Crossmatch(f, u)
  \/ \E f \in Fridges, u \in Units : IssueUnit(f, u)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_bankVars

\* Cold store, courier run, quarantine and issued always account between them
\* for exactly the units the bank started with: crating, taking off, cross-
\* matching and issuing move a unit, and never mint or lose one.
UnitsAreAccountedFor ==
  Cardinality(coldStore) + Cardinality(courierRun)
    + Cardinality(quarantine) + Cardinality(issued) = Cardinality(Units)
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Units = {bagO1, bagO2, bagA1}
    NumFridges = 3

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT UnitsAreAccountedFor
nl:
A hospital blood bank tracks numbered units of blood across several fridge stations. At any moment a unit is in exactly one of four places: sitting in the cold store, riding in a crate on the courier run between stations, waiting in quarantine for its crossmatch, or issued to a patient. Nothing is donated in and nothing is written off during the period being tracked, so the four places always account between them for exactly the units the bank started with.

The fridge stations take turns using a rota baton passed around them, and only the station currently holding the baton may touch the cold store: it alone may crate a unit up for the courier, bring a crossmatched unit back into store, or issue a unit out.

Crating a unit up takes it out of the cold store and turns it into exactly one crate on the courier run, tagged with the station that sent it. The courier run is a bag rather than a line: crates come off it in whatever order the courier happens to unload them, and a crate may sit on the run for an arbitrarily long time, so a crate posted later may well be taken off first. Taking a crate off the run puts its unit into quarantine. A crossmatch later moves a quarantined unit back into the cold store, and issuing takes a unit out of the cold store for a patient, which is where its tracking ends.

The full action set is: pass the rota baton to the next station, crate a cold-store unit up for the courier run, take any crate off the courier run and put its unit into quarantine, crossmatch a quarantined unit back into the cold store, and issue a cold-store unit to a patient.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The units in the cold store, the units riding on the courier run, the units in quarantine and the units already issued always add up to exactly the number of units the bank started with, so no unit of blood is ever duplicated or lost by crating, unloading, crossmatching or issuing, however the courier reorders the run.

----------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m3p5t4 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Cabins, MaxTerm, MaxLoading

Vacant == "vacant"

\* Blowing the traction isolator is a one-shot pyrotechnic act. Which cabin may
\* order it is settled by leader election: a failover opens a higher term and
\* voids every bid standing from the old one. Every bid, granted or refused,
\* is written into the incident ledger in the order it was settled.

VARIABLES term, chiefCabin, bid, isolator, loading, ledger
lineVars == <<term, chiefCabin, bid, isolator, loading, ledger>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ term \in 0 .. MaxTerm
  /\ chiefCabin \in Cabins \cup {Vacant}
  /\ bid \in [Cabins -> {"none", "raised", "settled"}]
  /\ isolator \in {"live", "blown"}
  /\ loading \in 0 .. MaxLoading

Init ==
  /\ term = 0
  /\ chiefCabin = Vacant
  /\ bid = [k \in Cabins |-> "none"]
  /\ isolator = "live"
  /\ loading = MaxLoading
  /\ ledger = <<>>

\* Failover. Bids standing from the old term are void, not carried over.
Failover(k) ==
  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ term' = term + 1
  /\ chiefCabin' = k
  /\ bid' = [j \in Cabins |-> "none"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<isolator, loading, ledger>>

\* The permitted loading of the line is retuned while the line is running.
Retune(n) ==
  /\ n # loading
  /\ loading' = n
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, chiefCabin, bid, isolator, ledger>>

RaiseBid(k) ==
  /\ bid[k] = "none"
  /\ bid' = [bid EXCEPT ![k] = "raised"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, chiefCabin, isolator, loading, ledger>>

\* Granted only for the chief of the live term, on a live isolator, and only
\* once the line has been wound right down to empty.
Blow(k) ==
  /\ bid[k] = "raised"
  /\ chiefCabin = k
  /\ isolator = "live"
  /\ loading = 0
  /\ isolator' = "blown"
  /\ ledger' = Append(ledger, [by |-> k, at |-> term, call |-> "granted"])
  /\ bid' = [bid EXCEPT ![k] = "settled"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, chiefCabin, loading>>

\* Every other raised bid is turned down, and the refusal is written down too.
Refuse(k) ==
  /\ bid[k] = "raised"
  /\ \/ chiefCabin # k
     \/ isolator = "blown"
     \/ loading > 0
  /\ ledger' = Append(ledger, [by |-> k, at |-> term, call |-> "refused"])
  /\ bid' = [bid EXCEPT ![k] = "settled"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<term, chiefCabin, isolator, loading>>

AnyBlow == \E k \in Cabins : Blow(k)
AnyRefuse == \E k \in Cabins : Refuse(k)

Next ==
  \/ \E k \in Cabins : Failover(k)
  \/ \E n \in 0 .. MaxLoading : Retune(n)
  \/ \E k \in Cabins : RaiseBid(k)
  \/ AnyBlow
  \/ AnyRefuse

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_lineVars
  /\ SF_lineVars(AnyBlow)
  /\ SF_lineVars(AnyRefuse)

\* A granted line closes the ledger for grants: every entry written after one
\* is a refusal, so the isolator is never ordered blown a second time however
\* the chief seat changes hands.
GrantClosesTheLedger ==
  \A i \in 1 .. Len(ledger) :
    ledger[i].call = "granted" =>
      \A j \in (i + 1) .. Len(ledger) : ledger[j].call = "refused"

EveryBidIsSettled ==
  \A k \in Cabins : (bid[k] = "raised") ~> (bid[k] # "raised")
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Cabins = {northcab, southcab}
    MaxTerm = 2
    MaxLoading = 1

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT GrantClosesTheLedger

PROPERTY EveryBidIsSettled
nl:
A subway line's block signalling system carries one pyrotechnic traction isolator. Blowing it cuts current to the whole line and is irreversible: the charge is spent, and no amount of work will put the isolator back. Because of that, deciding who may order it blown is settled by leader election among the signal cabins.

The line runs in numbered terms. A failover opens a higher term and installs a cabin as chief for it, and opening a new term voids every bid standing from the old term rather than carrying it forward. Separately, the permitted loading of the line -- how many trains the block system will admit -- is retuned while the line is running, up or down, right the way to empty.

Any cabin may raise a bid to blow the isolator. A bid is granted only when three things hold together: the bidding cabin is the chief of the live term, the isolator has not already been blown, and the line's permitted loading has been wound right down to empty. Every other raised bid is refused. Granted or refused, the outcome is written into the line's incident ledger in the order it was settled, recording which cabin bid, in which term, and what the answer was.

The full action set is: fail over to a new term with a named chief and void all standing bids, retune the line's permitted loading, raise a bid to blow the isolator, grant a bid by blowing the isolator and writing a granted line into the ledger, and refuse a bid and write a refused line into the ledger.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Once a granted line appears in the incident ledger, every entry written after it is a refusal, so the isolator is never ordered blown a second time however the chief seat changes hands or the loading is retuned.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every bid raised by a cabin is eventually settled, one way or the other, and never left standing forever.

----------------------------- MODULE W4Od16m4p4t4 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Scripts, MaxShelf, MaxBench

\* A script only joins the fill bench once a pigeonhole on the collection shelf
\* has been booked for it, so bench work and shelf stock are charged against
\* the same shelf rating. The pharmacist retunes both the bench depth and the
\* shelf rating during the day, but never below what is already committed.

VARIABLES bench, shelfStock, shelfRating, benchDepth, scriptAt
counterVars == <<bench, shelfStock, shelfRating, benchDepth, scriptAt>>

Committed == Len(bench) + shelfStock

TypeOK ==
  /\ shelfStock \in 0 .. MaxShelf
  /\ shelfRating \in 1 .. MaxShelf
  /\ benchDepth \in 1 .. MaxBench
  /\ scriptAt \in [Scripts -> {"lodged", "onbench", "onshelf", "collected"}]

Init ==
  /\ bench = <<>>
  /\ shelfStock = 0
  /\ shelfRating = 1
  /\ benchDepth = 1
  /\ scriptAt = [s \in Scripts |-> "lodged"]

\* Retuning down is allowed only as far as what is already committed.
RetuneShelf(n) ==
  /\ n # shelfRating
  /\ n >= Committed
  /\ shelfRating' = n
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bench, shelfStock, benchDepth, scriptAt>>

RetuneBench(n) ==
  /\ n # benchDepth
  /\ n >= Len(bench)
  /\ benchDepth' = n
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bench, shelfStock, shelfRating, scriptAt>>

\* Back pressure twice over: the bench must have room, and a pigeonhole on the
\* collection shelf must be free to book against this script.
TakeToBench(s) ==
  /\ scriptAt[s] = "lodged"
  /\ Len(bench) < benchDepth
  /\ Committed < shelfRating
  /\ bench' = Append(bench, s)
  /\ scriptAt' = [scriptAt EXCEPT ![s] = "onbench"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelfStock, shelfRating, benchDepth>>

\* Filling turns a booked pigeonhole into an occupied one: nothing is freed.
FillHead ==
  /\ Len(bench) > 0
  /\ scriptAt' = [scriptAt EXCEPT ![Head(bench)] = "onshelf"]
  /\ bench' = Tail(bench)
  /\ shelfStock' = shelfStock + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<shelfRating, benchDepth>>

HandOut(s) ==
  /\ scriptAt[s] = "onshelf"
  /\ shelfStock > 0
  /\ shelfStock' = shelfStock - 1
  /\ scriptAt' = [scriptAt EXCEPT ![s] = "collected"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<bench, shelfRating, benchDepth>>

Next ==
  \/ \E n \in 1 .. MaxShelf : RetuneShelf(n)
  \/ \E n \in 1 .. MaxBench : RetuneBench(n)
  \/ \E s \in Scripts : TakeToBench(s)
  \/ FillHead
  \/ \E s \in Scripts : HandOut(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_counterVars

\* The collection shelf is never oversubscribed: prescriptions already on the
\* shelf plus prescriptions on the bench with a pigeonhole booked for them
\* never together exceed whatever the shelf is rated at right now.
ShelfIsNeverOversubscribed ==
  Len(bench) + shelfStock <= shelfRating
================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Scripts = {rx101, rx102, rx103}
    MaxShelf = 2
    MaxBench = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT ShelfIsNeverOversubscribed
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser works lodged scripts through a fill bench and out onto a collection shelf. The collection shelf is the scarce resource: it has a rating saying how many prescriptions it can hold, and a prescription only leaves the shelf when a patient collects it.

The fill bench is a bounded work queue and it pushes back in two separate ways. A lodged script may only be taken to the bench if the bench is holding fewer scripts than its depth allows, and also only if a pigeonhole on the collection shelf can be booked for it there and then. That second check is the important one: shelf capacity is charged the moment a script joins the bench, not when the filled item finally lands on the shelf, so the bench and the shelf are counted against one shared rating.

Scripts are filled from the head of the bench in order. Filling moves the script off the bench and onto the shelf, which turns a booked pigeonhole into an occupied one and frees nothing. Handing a prescription out to the patient is what actually returns a pigeonhole to the shelf.

Neither limit is fixed for the day. The pharmacist retunes the shelf rating and the bench depth while the counter is open, but never downwards past what is already committed: the shelf rating is never set below the scripts on the bench plus the prescriptions on the shelf, and the bench depth is never set below what is already on the bench.

The full action set is: retune the shelf rating, retune the bench depth, take a lodged script to the bench while both the bench has room and a pigeonhole can be booked, fill the script at the head of the bench onto the shelf, and hand a shelved prescription out to its patient.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The prescriptions sitting on the collection shelf plus the scripts on the fill bench that already have a pigeonhole booked for them never together exceed whatever the shelf is rated at at that moment, however the pharmacist retunes the rating during the day.
